title: TE Trey McBride Minicamp Press Conference 06-09-26 | Arizona Cardinals 2026
text: You obviously came into the league with Cliff as your head coach, but it's been a few years since you had an offensive head coach and I'm just wondering what what's that been like? How much have you enjoyed the working with a guy who has his the offense background that Mike does? >> Yeah, it's really cool. Um, like you said that Cliff was there, but with GG, um, you know, offensive unit meetings and things, he wasn't really in there. He wasn't running the show. Um, you know, Petzing was doing that as he as a coordinator, but now, you know, with Mike, he's doing a great job of he's in there installing the plays. He's telling us exactly how he sees the routes done. He He's the one running the show and then Hackett kind of, you know, we'll we'll bounce ideas off of him, things like that, but it's really cool to hear it straight from the head coach what he wants, how he wants things done. And just to have an offensive head coach to to, you know, be able to get all these guys open and utilize the skill sets that we all have is pretty uh pretty special. >> How's the terminology coming? >> Yeah, you know, early on I was like, "Gosh, I'm I'm going to struggle learning this thing, but it's I I it's it's not bad at all. It's um after, you know, just like anything, you do it for a couple weeks, you kind of get better at it, you get more, you know, natural doing it and uh it's been awesome. Um, the his ability to get guys open, move people around and uh you know, the the play calls are hitting my brain perfectly right now. So, it's uh it's it's getting good. >> What are your favorite things about what this offense does? >> [clears throat] >> I just think it's a there's so much that it can do, you know, its ability to to marry up the run game and the pass game is is probably one of the most important things, you know, everything kind of looks the same. Whether you're running a run play, you're running a pass play, we're going to motion down, we're going to do the same things uh in both aspects. Maybe we're going to run a play action off of it and the next one we're going to run that the actual run. So, it's really cool to see how he's able to utilize that, how he's able to move people around, get into 12 personnel, 13 personnel, do the same thing that we're doing um in 11 personnel, but just do it with a few more tight ends on the field. So, his ability to to move people around, get people open is is pretty fun. >> There's There's a general uncertainty in terms of what's going to happen at quarterback. You got a lot of a lot of options. Um how do you kind of maneuver through that right now? Or do you even have to since it's not even training camp? >> Yeah, I mean um honestly, early on in this, I was just trying to learn the playbook, trying to you know, figure out what I was doing and uh as long as I'm getting open and and and doing my job, I feel like whoever's throwing the ball is going to be able to get it to me. I you know, Jacoby came back today. It was cool to see him in you know, his presence, just how everyone feels about him, things like that. So, it's good to have him, but really whoever's back there, man, we're going to get open and uh feel like one of you guys can throw if if we get open, you know. >> How does everyone feel about him? >> About what? >> Jacoby. >> Jacoby. I mean, I feel like guys are excited that he was here. Guys want him to be here. Um obviously would love to have him in the building, but he's working through some things on his own. So, we totally understand that, but you could just tell the presence that he brought today being in in the building was was awesome. >> Coach was just saying about Coach was just saying about how with every player like even if you were great last year, which you were, like that's gone now. Is that easy for you to kind of >> Yeah, no. >> mentally like that's gone now? >> Yeah, that's how I feel about it every year. It's like the slate's clean. You got to prove it every single year. It's like whatever you did last year, great, but no one really cares. Like it's it's a new year, it's a new chapter, new coach, new everything. So, it's like you just got to keep bringing it every year. You got to be the You got to just be a little bit better than what you were last year and and what makes a great player is just the consistency of of doing it year in and year out and not having these big highs and big lows. You just have to keep keep going, keep going and just try to be a little bit better than you were the year before. >> You mentioned kind of this offense's ability to do different things out of the same look, but also then do the same thing out of different looks, different different personnel groupings. It makes sense to do the benefit of doing different things out of the same look to confuse the picture for defenses. What's the benefit of being able to do the same thing out of different looks and different personnel groupings? What does that do for the offense? >> I mean, it probably screws the defense up more than anything where you're motioning down and you're inserting a guy to block a safety. And then you're motioning a guy down, now you're inserting him, he's fake blocking, now he's running a corner. And and for the defense, it looks the exact same for them. They're look like, is he blocking me? Is he going to run by me? What's the deal? So, I think it presents more of a challenge on the defense than it does changing anything we do. We're just going to be really good at what we do and then present different looks to the defense and hopefully screw them up a little bit and catch them off guard and be able to, you know, get a cheap one. >> You've been one of the most consistent players you talk about. And then during last season, I mean, I guess two seasons ago, what you were coming off of, you were garnering a lot more attention than you had. Last year from the coaching staff, we heard maybe one of the biggest improvements to that adjustment was reading defenses better. What have you been working on or what's your goal the rest of the off-season as you all continue to garner more attention with how you play? >> Yeah, I feel like just the like you said, the way you're reading defenses, every team plays you a little bit different, whether they're chipping you at the line, whether they're, you know, have a safety over the top, but really identifying who's covering you and how, you know, your route affects you know, who's covering you and um I think that's something I've gotten better at and I'm still trying to get better at is who's who's who am I trying to beat on this play and you know, how much free will do I have to beat this guy and being able to digest that as fast as I can and be able to to play at a high level, play fast is is very important and I just try to run fast and and get open and you know, hopefully the ball finds me and more often than not it does. >> What you were talking about running back room all considered and if a couple guys getting healthy again, what that room could be like for you guys again this >> I mean, it's it's definitely the best running back room I've been a part of I think since I've been in the NFL. It's you know, Jeremiah's a stud. There's a reason why he's the third overall pick. His just ability to get open and and you know, make things happen not only in the run game but in the pass game as well. Obviously, James Conner's a proven guy, a guy who's been on this team, been a high, you know, workhorse guy for us, a stud player. Trey Benson's another guy, second round pick, you know, you draft him high for a reason. I think he's still flourishing into who he can become. And then you got TA, Tyler. I mean, he's a proven guy too that that's been playing at a high level the last couple years. So, just with those four guys alone, I mean, we still got a few other guys, but those four guys alone there's a lot of power, there's a lot of trust, there's a lot of proven guys in that and they're all just different in their own ways and they all have different skill sets and I'm just excited to keep them going. They're just a workhorse, you know, unit and I'm excited to block for those guys and see how how powerful they can be. >> What have you seen from the >> Same as the running back room that I have >> been seeing a lot of improvement from Elijah Higgins. He even looks bigger. What have you seen of him since you've been sharing the room with him? >> Yeah, Higgy's a a stud, man. He's a guy who's selfless. He's a guy who does everything the coach asks of him and uh I I truly do love playing with him. This is I think my fourth season with him now. So, it's pretty cool to see how we've grown together, how you know, the two of us have have played well together and he's a guy that that probably doesn't get enough attention. He's a really good player, a guy who can probably do a lot of the same stuff I do but it's really cool to watch him, how he's developed over the years. He's a tremendous player and I'm excited to see how he continues to grow this year. >> Trey, last year Marvin had some nice moments but he also had some really bad luck with injuries. How How do you think we are from seeing him at his best? >> I think we're right there. Um, you know, Marvin's a stud. He's a guy who's probably one of the hardest workers I've seen. A guy who does everything the right way and um, yeah, he got a little, you know, banged up last year and that's a bummer. Uh, just with his, you know, injury history, he's never really been hurt. So, I'm excited to, you know, have him back, get him back on the field cuz when he's on the field, defenses have to be aware of where he's at and what he's doing cuz he's a guy who can wreck a game and and he's a huge asset for us. So, um, I would love to have him back at full going. Uh, you know, obviously he's still getting back whatever he's doing, but he's a he's had a great, you know, OTAs and I'm excited to see him continue to grow. >> You talking about getting open and reading the defenses who's covering you, but how much of that too is the complimentary routes with the other receivers that are downfield? How much you have to be aware of spacing and >> Yeah. Yeah, and that's the thing, you know, we got a lot of selfless guys who do a lot of stuff to to help me get open and I and that doesn't go unrecognized where maybe they're running deep to get the safety out of there then I'm coming, you know, on an underneath route, whatever it may be, but um, those guys do a great job of of getting me open too. Um, it's not just me, you know, running routes. Those guys are have a huge part of that too, but yes, I'm very aware of how much room I have to work, where the other guys are, uh, what their routes are as well just so I know, you know, my area to get open and uh, you know, I feel like I've done a good job about that and I just want to continue getting better, too. >> What do you think Michael Wilson's emergence will do for you this year? >> Yeah, um, man, Mike's a stud. He's a guy who um, just is one of the hardest working guys I know, too. He's he's proven he I mean, just the way he practices, it's full go every time and uh, he's a tremendous player, a guy who, uh, defenses will be, uh, you know, more tuned into what he's doing this year. He's a guy that can wreck a game, too. Um, so, his ability to to split out and you know, take coverage to that side, whatever could it could also help me out as well. So, the two of us together, um, I think could be a you know a great you know tandem this year, but I'm excited to to see Mike emerge into another great season. >> When we talk about the spacing with the other receivers, having such consistency across the board, especially with the starters on this offense, is that a place where you can see that chemistry carry over or not so much because as long as you know the playbook and you know which route to run? >> No, I think there's a lot a lot of chemistry with that as well. Knowing how guys run routes, maybe you know how they get open, things like that, and knowing you know who's out there definitely makes a difference in how you approach that play. Um but I think just continuing to get reps with each other, continuing to to build as a as an offense, as a team, I think that's just going to keep you know heading in the right direction and I'm excited to see where it goes. >> How have you seen that Kendrick Bourne kind of fit into the equation here? >> Yeah, he's a he's he's awesome, man. He's full of energy. He's always smiling. You know, he's the life of the the huddle, whatever you want to say. He's uh he's awesome, but um his uh his emergence, man, he's a selfless guy, too. He's an he's a guy who is able to catch a ton of balls, but he's you know doing all the the other stuff, blocking, doing the the dirty work, but he's a tremendous player as well, and I'm excited to see you know his addition to to the offense and and his ability to make plays as well. >> Kittle, let your hair grow a little bit. Don't judge Kittle. >> Yeah, no, not I don't know about that, but it is getting a little long, man. I don't know what what's going on. I I haven't had long hair in a long time, so I'm kind of just just letting it go. >> Kittle was [snorts] just in here talking about some comparison and contrast with you and George Kittle's game. He had more coming towards Kittle before. Says you guys are cut from the same cloth. What do you feel like kind of that same cloth is that you guys each share that same mentality? >> Yeah, I just think you know to play the tight end position, it's um it's just a lot of want to and and willingness to do it. And his ability to get open in the pass game, it really starts in the the game. Like you have to be able to block to play tight end like I know I catch a ton of balls, but you have to block in this league. You have to be able to put your hand in the dirt and and get down and get gritty. Like, that it's just it's part of the game and um and I think that's something you know, before I was catching all the balls, that's what I was doing. I I was a blocking guy. I did a lot of that stuff. So, I think that's, you know, where it starts is being able to to want to and have that willingness to to get down and get dirty and do that stuff and then that's what opens up you in the passing to get open and and be able to do that. But, the tight end position is just a lot of want to and that's what it boils down to.

title: Dave Canales wraps up mandatory minicamp | Carolina Panthers
text: Good morning. >> Thank you so much for taking the time to talk to us. >> Absolutely. You got it. >> Would you like to start off with an opening statement? >> Uh, sure. U, you know, we were scheduled to have a practice today. Um, challenge the guys on Tuesday, you know, as far as just, you know, it was a good hard practice and I just like we got more in the tank and yesterday we had some of the highest outputs we've had uh from guys just finishing plays, hustling, uh, high speed yardage, all those things. And um just felt like coming into today, you know, that the best thing we could do is to capitalize on a great spring, get the guys in for a meeting. Um you know, talk about the uh just, you know, challenging the guys to have a plan uh for these next five weeks. As you can imagine, you know, that time goes quickly while it is valuable for all of us. Um you know, there's this season that we're really excited about. Um and uh the group feels that way. The energy is is in the right place. Um they're challenging each other, accountable to each other, and and the work this this uh offseason has been fantastic. We're in great shape right now. Um we need to maintain that and make sure that we can come back to a camp that's going to be the hardest camp they've ever had and uh we have joint practices. You know, we got an extra preseason game and that's going to that's going to challenge us in new ways. So um just wanted to make sure they knew that on the front end. You know, we got to be ready to go when you come back in. Nine practices and we're playing the Hall of Fame game. So, um it was a good opportunity to connect that way for them to connect with each other, with their position coaches, um and just talk about their plan. And as you can imagine, there are veterans who have a plan. They have a rhythm of what they do. And there are rookies who have never had this type of uh off time where typically they're working out at the school and they have scheduled workouts and and with with things being less structured, you got to have structure to have consistency. And so, it was a great day to take advantage of that. and um and we're excited to uh you know take this time, take advantage and come back ready to go. >> All right, we'll kick things off with Mike K followed by Scott Fowler. >> Hey Dave, good morning. >> Morning. I know Brandt and Dan are going to handle contracts and contract extensions, but what is your personal philosophy when a guy has viewed his contract like he's out overperformed it and wants an extension and you're getting into the thick of game planning and you're you're thinking about culture uh coming into potentially a new season we saw with Taylor Moden getting his extension last year. I'm just curious what's your what's your point of view in that entire process and how are you involved? >> Absolutely. Uh it's a great question and for Dan and I and Brent, we're all on the same page with trying to identify guys that are Panther football players and yes, a huge component of that is the production on the field and first and foremost, right? That's how the market is set across the league. Um, but beyond that, we want guys to be here long term that embody what we're looking for in terms of play style, character on and off the field. Guys that are great teammates, um, guys that take personal accountability and responsibility for their job and are always prepared and show up with that type of work mentality and mindset and the way that they practice, how hard they practice, guys that find their way to be available because they take care of themselves. Um, so we factor all those things in, but like for the long-term commitment, it's got to be guys that we believe embody what we're trying to build here and what we're trying to maintain and establish as a cultural um, identity. And so all of those factors go into it. My contribution obviously is for guys how they fit into specific schemes um, and how we've adjusted our schemes because they bring something special or not. So, from a football production standpoint, and then of course it's all of us putting our heads together in terms of, you know, at some point it gets harder and harder. You can't pay everybody and [clears throat] we're going to have to have some really, you know, challenging um conversations and and challenging decisions to be made. The longer we're here, the longer we're building this team to say, okay, we have multiple guys who kind of embody what we're looking for. And then you have to make those decisions and that all has to fit in from a salary cap standpoint and that's where you know Brent does such a brilliant job of piecing the the whole thing together. >> And then uh Thomas Turk and Icky will they I know you don't want to give timelines on those guys but will they begin training camp on Pop? >> We'll see. I don't know. I'm not going to give anything specific on all those. Okay. >> Hey Dave, uh two quick things. One just off what you just said. When you say it's going to be the hardest camp they've ever had, are you talking from a physical standpoint? Are you saying basically because they have an extra preseason game or is there something else? Are you, you know, doing something different in this camp compared to the last two? >> Yeah, a big part of it is the nature of um having the extra game, having multiple joint practices, which we we've done. Um but just knowing the preparation that it takes in those days and then of course just when you have high intensity um either joint practice or you have a high intensity preseason game, the the challenge is in the recovery part of it, making sure that guys stay on top of taking care of their body so we can turn right back around and throw another great week of practice. um maximizing the time that we're on the field, making sure that you know we're however we do it, we're maximizing time on grass. And [clears throat] um while we'll be smart and we will, you know, fluctuate the the tempos of the practice and and we'll take in all the information, we're going to try to maximize our time out there. And and for me, I think it's really just the nature of where we're at. Every year, we're trying to push the envelope. Every year we're trying to do things smarter and harder if it needs to be, but just the nature of having familiarity with our schemes allows us to go faster into our schemes. Um, add a little bit a few more wrinkles. So, there's a mental strain that comes along with this requires even a little bit more studying because we're going to do this same play, but now we're doing it out of a different personnel or a different shift in motion on the defensive side. having multiple adjustments by formation with different pressures or different calls um and just challenging the guys that way so that we can just continue to make our um to diversify our schemes and all that. So, it's it's all-encompassing. There's a physical component, there's a component that's um going to happen because of the schedule, the scheduling that we have, and then there's of course the mental component that we just talked about. >> Thanks. And the other one just quickly, um what do you expect from Tommy Trimble this year? What do you want from him? >> Tommy has had a great spring. Um, Tommy's worked through some things physically over the last two seasons. He's had as healthy of a spring as I've seen him. He looks fast. Um, I know I know he's a physical player. We're not in pads, so I know that part will still come alive. Um, and I just think with his familiarity with our system and how to use the tight end position, um, how to isolate guys in different positions on linebackers or safeties and things like that. Um, Tommy's done such a great job this spring. I really expect to see great things from him. >> Thank you. >> We'll go with Nick Carboni followed by Joe Pson and Jeff Hawkins. >> Good morning, Dave. Apologize for the cam >> camera issue today, but wanted to ask you saw saw you spend quite a bit of time with T-Mac yesterday as he wasn't practicing and having, you know, lengthy conversations. What are you kind of picking up from him right now in terms of, you know, trying to figure out the craft better and what are those conversations with him like? >> Team really locked in um tracking with all of our concepts. One of the things we learned about him early on as a rookie is his ability to retain information. um the smallest of details in the pass game in splits, who to block, he picks it up quickly. Um he's in he's so into it and he just has a special mind for how he's able to incorporate all the information we give him into his play and maintain a speed of play. I'm really excited for him. Just um he looks great physically. You know, he's as strong as he's ever been. He's as fast as he's ever been. Um he's really spent a lot of time training and taking care of his body, getting stronger. um getting faster, a lot of the things that he really wanted to focus on. And uh you know, as he continues to do those things, as we get him back out there on the grass, there's a leadership component that comes with it. He's a man of few words, but it's the guy that it's the guys that practice hard every day. He attacks the ball. He finishes every catch with the run after catch or even if no one's out there, he's imagining someone's there. It's all those practice habits. Those are the things that we look for in terms of our practice culture and trying to steal a game rep is what we talk about. And you can use your imagination to really get your body into a game type of setting without having it be, you know, full contact and all those things. And and that's something special that he brings. I'm just looking for him to continue to bring that type of professionalism to the grass um so that we can all continue to refine our craft. >> Hey Dave, good to see you. >> Hey Joe. on uh for the most part the last few weeks we saw the rookies and the draft picks uh work with the second and third teams. Uh maybe Will Lee being the exception. Was that a product of like not wanting to hand a a first team job to to to a high draft pick in the case of like a Freeling or where where does that position battle stand would you say and and just your philosophy in general with those with those rookies? Yeah. So, my philosophy in general is I want our rookies to play and I want them to um be exposed to being with the first groups. We've sprinkled them in there at this in this phase right now. As you can imagine, they're they come into it a few weeks behind most of the other guys who are operating at a pretty high level with our schemes and concepts. Even guys like Rasheed who came from another team with a very similar run game, very similar pass protection scheme, play action schemes, those types of things. There's a lot to gain for a young guy to watch a veteran player who's been in a system like ours to see how it's done, where they put their body, where they put their hands, how they get off on the snap. Um, all those little things you can pick up a lot by standing back and watching a guy do it. Um, also I don't want to hold back a group that's ready to go because of guys that might not be ready right away. Um, and that's all across the board. That's on offense, defense, and special teams. We don't want to hold our team back in this phase from getting really good examples on film. So, we have the guys who know how to do it, who've been here. So, we can show these cutups. you'll see it live, but then when you watch it happen, you see this is how we want it done. So, it does accelerate the learning curve. And as we are able to stack more time in training camp, it becomes very critical that the guys that show that they may have a chance to help this team have an opportunity to be out there with the first group so they can feel the pressure of, okay, I know the least in this huddle. I got to make sure I study. I got to make sure my stuff is right. I got to make sure my technique is right. And I'm not letting the whole group down by my play. I like that urgency. We will give those guys those opportunities as we go into camp with the first group to see how they respond. And that's where guys are able to make an impression and make an impact. And um and that's the nature of competition. And you can imagine what that does to a guy that has been doing a little bit better, but all of a sudden this other guy gets a couple of reps and it's like I got to go. I got to take my game up a little bit. And so it's the nature of competition. I believe in it. I think it makes the whole thing better. >> And then specifically, what would you say you've seen from Monroe Freeling over the past couple months? >> Yeah. Uh, steady growth. Um, you know, every every week, new installs with our rookies now. We've been able to go through the install twice. Um, so they have a good amount of exposure. I've seen him learn how fast this thing moves up front and what it's like to try to block Derrick Brown on the backside of a run and how right that first step has to be. I've also seen him be really comfortable in space and pass bro because of how big and athletic he is. Holds a point in the run game when we run at him. Um we see all the physical attributes and the reason why we took him in the first round. Those things are all there. He's having a great time. He loves to play football. I didn't know that about him. That was a pleasant surprise to see just kind of the joy that he plays with. Even when he makes a mistake, he handles it with a lot of humility, a lot of grace, and he's like, "I'll get it the next time." But there's not a lot of panic there um with him. And so, a guy that takes pride in his work, but is also understands like these are things I'm working through. Um and uh I'm I'm I just have watched I'm just learning who the guy is, you know, and and I'm excited that he's here. >> And then, sorry, real quickly, uh when will you report? >> Uh July 22nd. Thank you. Have a good summer. Thank you. >> Greetings, coach. How are you? >> Hey, Jeff. >> Hey, hope you have a good couple weeks. Thank you. >> Yeah, I just spoke with JT Sanders and uh he mentioned that the time off he had after the injury was actually a blessing. Um he's he's no longer taking the game for gr the game for granted and it gave him time to work on fundamentals. Uh have you seen a difference in him mentally? Um, and physically entering his third year, >> I thought JT did an excellent job going into the 2025 off season. Um, he looked faster, he looked stronger, he knew our stuff, a really smart guy. He's into it. He studies. I've seen him replicate that process and throw another great spring. Um, this is the type of consistency that we're looking for from our guys. Um to your point, I've noticed a guy that really enjoys being out there with his teammates and competing and that um he's always kind of had that good energy, but I can feel that there's just a uh a level of comfortability, a guy that's emerging as a leader on our team because of how he prepares and how he contributes on offense and on special teams. He understands how important it is um all these phases for winning games and for playing really good football. So, a guy that I really lean on, a guy that I'm I'm so proud that he's here because he sets that example of what we're looking for from Panther football players. >> And I just want a quick follow up on Freeling. Um, over the over the OTAAS, I I I seen Nick and Princeley uh beat him pretty badly on on outside speed rushes. Um, is that one move he needs to work on? Is it a first step uh um issue or um is it just growing pains? Well, first of all, give Nick and Princely their due. These are guys that that are running into their second offseason and two really talented players, which is exactly what we want. This is what we talk about. We make us. We make us right on the practice field. And it's guys going 100 miles an hour challenging each other with different moves, different things to expose the things we need to work on and to hone our craft. And that's exactly what Monroe needs right now is to just go against guys like that. going against Jaylen Phillips and going against Pat Jones who's a veteran guy who's got all the moves and the setups and these are things and these are get offs and moves and things that you know he saw some he saw some really good talent played against some really good talent you know over the last two years but um you know to face that every day in this setting is is so good for him right now. >> Hey, thanks. Enjoy your time. >> Thanks Jeff. >> We'll go with Cass and end with Mike K. >> Hey Dave, how's it going? >> Hey Cass. >> Uh sorry my camera is not working either. I know we've talked about the the the growth on the offensive side of the ball and then being able to kind of take more ownership, but on the defensive side, particularly with that triangle of players of like JC, Nick Scott, Mike, Jack, how have obviously they know the system and have played in it, but having seen them play together the last couple of years, how have they sort of grown together and what sort of freedom does that give them within the defense? like obviously not ignoring or EJ's calls, but what sort of freedom does that just give them to to grow and to to help everyone around them, I guess, as well? >> Yeah. Well, you forgot to mention the jackhammer Trey Merrick, too. So, that's a >> Exactly. >> It's a really good group. It's a veteran group that trust each other and have spent a lot of time communicating, getting calls across the board. Um, with any given call, there are adjustments to formations. There are adjustments to um the area of the field. There are all these uh intricacies that have to be communicated really quickly as the offense is taking the line of scrimmage and that's where I've seen the biggest growth um the biggest jump. You really saw it happen mid-season last year and you saw a group really play together um all the way through the end of the season and pick right back up in the offseason. What a great group for guys like Will Leaf, for guys like Zaki Wheatley um to see, you know, and then you talk about Shaw Smith Wade, you talk about Corey Thornton. Um these are guys that really know what we're doing as well. And the communication that happens across the board with that group has been incredible. Um it's a great room. It's a great room of guys that care about, they're conscientious. I believe we have the best of the best in terms of training our players right here in our building. We got the facilities and all the resources right on hand. That's what I want. That's what he wants for our group. So, I'm excited for that. And then, of course, just going into it, um, how many call it periods can I expose Brad to? You know, going into these preseason games, challenging him with different situations, making it so that he can see as this play clock goes, you got to have a plan for the next play. This could be a fourth down go. This could also be a first and 10. And having the um having the mental gymnastics to handle all those and still maintain a flow of what you're trying to present to the defense, all that rhythm. That's the part that I'll be really connected with and and watch him as we go into camp. >> All right, coach. Thank you so much for taking the time to talk to us this morning. >> All right. title: Christian Jones and Ephraim Banda Press Conference | June 11th, 2026
text: It looks like uh your rookies have really come on strong over the past even couple of weeks. Can you just talk about how they're doing? >> That's a great question. Um I think the rookies have done a good job. It's really about understanding the concepts, understanding the plays and really it's learning the playbook. After that, they're able to play fast. Once you get them to understand the plays and how to do things the right way, you know, it's it's their time for their talents to shine. They've done a good job. And Casey came in the right mindset. you know, he was ready to work on what he thought was an issue coming in the draft, which which were his drops. Denzel wanted to show everybody what he could do. He was really, you know, upset about where the draft landed and they've come out and done a really good job. I'm proud of him. >> I remember talking to you last spring and talking about you had like maybe one charted drop for Harold and it seems like Denzel has had a similar spring like does he just catch everything basically in his radius? >> He has done a good job. Now, he had one day he came out and he was a little off, but he's done a really good job with catching the ball, finishing. Really, it's just seeing into the tough, but you talk about where they put the ball, where he goes for it. I mean, he's not afraid to go get it. And really, the impressive thing with a lot of the guys is they're not afraid to go use their hands. Like, a lot of guys like let it come to the body sometimes, and he's not afraid to go snatch it, pluck it out there, and pull it. So, been really good to see. >> Is it fair to expect those two rookies to have an immediate impact when we get when you get to the season? Expectations are great, but it's all about the work they put in. I think we all expect that from them. That's the standard we're going to hold them to, but it's always up to them on what they're going to be able to do and what they want to do themselves. So, my job is to get the best out of them. That's my goal for them. And that's what we're going to try to achieve. But the onus is always on me to get them there and on them to want to attain it. >> How have you seen Jerry kind of come back this year after all those struggles last year, drops and things like that? How have you seen how have you seen him come back? >> Mindset's been great. Mindset has been great. I mean, he comes in every day prepared, knows what to do, asks questions in the meeting room. Um, helping the young guys understand how to run routes, the intricate points with releases. I mean, he's been great. He's a leader in the room. Wants guys to understand what to do cuz he understands it helps him. And him getting play, him playing well helps them. The them playing well helps him. It all works together. >> Coach, coach Monin broke into the league as a receivers's coach, right? He seems to be very handson with that position. Why is that? I think it's exactly what you said, right? He started as a receivers's coach. So, there's always going to be that passion for wanting to coach that group and it's been great. I've always wanted to learn from somebody that does really well with coaching receivers. And there's never you can never you never learn enough about the position. I'm always trying to learn and get better. So, being able to work with somebody who's done it for so long, coach that room for so long, and is not afraid to get out there and do it himself, has been great. with all the pre- snap motion. >> Is there more responsibility on his receivers and his offense? >> Absolutely. Absolutely. But I think the the more responsibility the better. I mean, there's there's more onus on us to know what to do and how to do it and really be good at it, right? Um and be detailed. And I mean, I I take it as a privilege, right? We should be prideful of that. And I think that's how we try to approach it. >> You mentioned coach uh Isaiah last year. Was it good to be able to see him now that you're like him on a daily basis? What's what's different about him now? >> Um, I can't say it was different because I didn't have too many interactions with him, but I can say that um what he has done is come in with a great mindset. He tries to learn, ask questions. He's not afraid to ask questions at all. I mean, we could be two plays down, he'll ask me to go back to make sure he's got something down. And at least that's on the field. You know, a lot of fast receivers typically have issues getting in and out of their brakes, carrying their speed into their brakes, and that's something that I have not seen without. He's not afraid to carry all his speed into a speed cut, coming back down his stem, an angle break, a square cut, and that's been really impressive. >> He talked to us yesterday about that he's added 15 lbs of muscle this off season and he wants to, you know, up his versatility since everyone always talks about his speed. Like, how has that added strength showed up in his game on the field so far? It's a lot harder to push him off the spot now. We've got to get him to start using that a little bit more when he's running his routes and he's run these go routes and everything, but you see it in his releases. You can see it in how he plays. He's not afraid to go up and attack the ball. He's not afraid to get guys off of him when he's running his routes. And I think he'll show up in the run game, especially when he put pads on. So, it's been great to see. >> Sorry, you mentioned you mentioned it with Casey, and I know he mentioned it when he first got here that he wants to work on the the drops that he had in college. What are some of the ways that you kind of get into the the nitty-gritty maybe with him on fixing that and trying to make that something that he can improve? >> Sure. I think what I try to focus on it's it probably goes back to something you do in day one when you're playing receiver is looking the ball into the tuck. A lot of receivers catch it. A lot of concentration drops come when they catch it. They start looking to see who they got to make miss where they're going down the field. And that's where the ball tends to fall out because on the way to the tuck, they lose sight of it or they lose control of it. So, it's always seeing it into the tuck and then adding distractions into every catch, every drill that we have, we try to have some kind of distraction. So, soon as we do that, I think it makes everything a little bit easier for them. And you just try to build the routine and turn that into a habit. >> How eager are you to see um especially maybe the rookies go up against a Denzel Ward and a Grand Delit when those guys rejoin practice? >> I can't wait. I can't wait. I told Denzel that uh two days ago when he first got back that I was so excited he was back so I could see, you know, how our guys are going to play against him. It's been great going against Tyson and I'm excited to see them going against the both of them at the same time. I'm really excited to see how they'll develop going against two different profiles of corners. I'm excited for that. >> You talked about the added responsibility that the receivers have Todd's offensive. Uh is there a big change in the emphasis on what routes they're running from a year ago to this system? I would say it's a great question. I would say with different systems, there's an emphasis on different types of routes and the different break points that certain systems have, right? Certain system, some systems lean on curls where you have an angle breaker coming back to the quarterback. So, a lot more their angles might be coming quarterback. Some may be more based on breaking out. Some may be more based on sitting down at the top. So I think in this system um we've been leaning more towards like stay we like to stay on the move. We will break down to come back to the quarterback. We use a lot of different breaks use a lot of different break points and it's really about us being detailed in those points whether it's off or press and you can see us when we do routes on air we really try to give the best look we can for every break point versus every look. So, we use every single break that we have and I say there's a lot of variation in what we do to keep defenses guessing and I think that's something that's really good for us and it's on us now to understand the details so when we hear called we can execute that. >> What type of impression has Tylen Wallace made um on your practice like always in practice? >> Uh Tylen's been great. Uh I've been leaning on Tylen in the meetings every time I had a question and I didn't have the time to ask Monk. So, anytime something came up, I asked Tylen. So, it's been great to have them in there. He's been helping me. Um, and really he's just been doing a good job of making plays. He shows up when you ask him to go do something, knows what to do, does it full speed, and he's been a great resource. >> Boston impacted him. His strong hands were jumped in as advertised and contested catch and all that, but he looks more fluid for a big guy than advertisers. Is that fair to say running rounds? I can say that I wish I would have been able to see him do something before um we drafted him in person, but >> it's been pleasant. I've been pleasantly surprised. That's always the the worry you have when some guys come in. But from the first day we watched some routes, I mean, it was jog through and I was like, "This guy's got great hips. He knows what to do." And he's really focused on doing that and being good on every aspect of his game and he knows what his issues are and what to work on. So, >> what are his issues? Um, it's just what you say. When you're taller, it's a lot harder to get in your break. You got a lot more room to get down. It takes you a lot longer to get down, right? And so when you're playing that spot, that's always something that's difficult for guys who are 6'4 or taller. So that's always going to be difficult for them. And so he's been a good he's done a good job working on it and understand how to get better at it. And really coming, he came in having already worked on it himself. So what I love about it is he's selfled. He wants to get better and he does it himself too, right? and that makes a lot easier on me as a coach to um supplement his growth. >> What's the biggest change or adjustment for you transitioning from tight end coach to vars coach working with a larger group? Maybe some different personalities. What's that been like that change like for you? >> These guys, every receiver we have in that room is great. So, there hasn't been any issues with personalities. They're all great. They always they all want to be great. I would say there's a lot more guys to have to work with and manage. Um so, I've had to lean on people a lot more. more. I try to do things a lot. I have to do things a lot myself, but I've gotten better at using the resources around me. We got a great player development department. We got Demetri Felton who helps us out with a lot with our receivers. My assistant receivers, coach, John Waznjak, helps me a lot. Um, that's the first thing. I would say the second thing is the amount of detail I had to have for running routes. I think that's something that's always I would say it stepped it to another level, especially when Monk came in with how much he's done himself and how much experience he has with it. So, I just try to be I try to like ask him any question I have. He's an open book, so I take every resource I can use from him. >> Thank y'all. Thank you very much. Yeah. >> Thank you. Have a good day. Thank you. Good. >> Good. Y'all have a good day. Settle. Yeah, there you go. Love it. Summer is finally here. >> Took a while though. >> Who's going first? >> Well, let's start with the Delta. >> Okay. >> Obviously not out there. Yeah. >> Yeah. I mean, obviously can't speak on injuries, won't the biggest thing I would say is just really proud of his his um communication in the offseason's been phenomenal. Uh his time in the building has been great. Working hard, being present, you know, doing a great job in meetings, being a veteran leader, you know, I think he's the second longest tenure Brown now, uh if I'm not mistaken, or or on defense if I'm not mistaken. So, great to have him around. Love him. Uh he's been a it's been good. We're going on year four together now. So it's been really good to have that. Did a really good job this off seasonason again just um checking in and staying with his communication and been great in the in the room. >> How about you? Talk about what you're seeing from him so far and what you think the upside potential can be. >> Just really impressed with his diligence in the room, you know, in the in the study area and the walkers. He hasn't had a ton of time obviously due to what happened in spring, but um you know in those situations when you get a rookie in that like things can go either way. He's done a great job of staying locked in, spending a bunch of time with our professional development or our development department, getting extra time, extra meetings, just being very present and learning to be a pro, building a routine. He's got a great room around him that can help him do that. So excited about the training camp portion. I've told him, you got to be ready to go when it's time. How difficult is that not having two of your top three guys for pretty much most of the offense? >> Uh kind of gotten used to it over the years, right? You know, you think about year one, year two, year three. Uh but what's come of that is uh a lot of other guys getting reps in the development of the room, which you know, really proud of over the last few years. So guys like Chris Edmonds have got a ton of reps and had a great spring. Uh you know, Donovan McMillan, same thing. Those guys have really reaped the benefits of that. It's not easy, but it does help you when the season gets long and you have injuries and things that go on. Those guys are more aptable to play. And you've seen that over the last few years. The guys have been able to come in and help us, which will happen. >> So, when we get to camp, training camp, will will Emanuel compete for free safety or will he be the third safety? >> You know, to be determined, the biggest thing I would say is, you know, to echo what AB said, you know, we want to crawl first, walk, then run. I don't want to put him in a situation where it could be too much if I bop him around too much. I'll do something similar to what I did with Rocket. Start somewhere, let him get real comfortable, feet wet, see if he's good, not really get to the running part yet. And you know, I say run like adding extra stuff uh to his plate. Um, but I'm excited to see where he can fit in this scheme with the ability to play with multiple safeties, which we've done. So to be determined unfortunately to get a chance to do a lot of it. I will say the mental aptitude and where he what he's done in there is encouraging and I can't wait to see what he can do on the field but we need to get him out there and let him spill the milk a little bit you know and which we didn't get a ton of time to do this year this spring. >> You have an idea. >> You are obviously here with with Jim. Now Mike comes in. Just maybe what are some of the differences in in terms of what you've seen working with him versus what you've sort of seen the last few years working with you? The first thing I'll say is I've been blessed in both situations. You know, working for Jim was phenomenal. I mean, he's uh one of the best defensive coordinators this league's ever seen and I learned a ton and I grew a ton. Um he did it his way and he was hard fast hard and set in his ways and you respect that. With Rudy, same, you know, he's a super brilliant coach, but he's himself and I respect that too. He is who he is. He's not shy to be that. It's been amazing to get around that. His energy is phenomenal. His uh his his willingness to listen and also apply things that we bring up and talk about. It's been great. Um I love that, you know, I give a ton of credit. He's came in here, he could easily changed everything on the defense, but he didn't. He gets a he he deserves a ton of respect for keeping things as as much as he can the same for the players and coaches, and I respect that. And also his willingness to listen to things that we want to mess with or change or make better. and also just looking at the things from outside and say, "Hey, can could we do this a little differently?" So, it's been great to have him. Uh, his energy is phenomenal. It's been fun to work with him. >> When there's a change like that, you I'm sure it's like hard to know like what your future sort of holds, too. So, what what did it mean for them to sort of value you and and want to keep you here along with some of the other positions on that side of the ball? >> Look, at the end of the day, the Cleveland Browns organization took a chance on me almost four years ago, and I am very very indebted to that. And again, when this came situation came up, they still told me exactly how they felt with their actions. And I have a ton of respect and admiration to that. And I for that, I am all in to be a Cleveland Brown for as long as this organization will have me. So, I am very thankful for the HLMS. I'm very thankful for Kevin in the past and coach Monkin now and and Rudy and the other in the and the other parts of this organization, D and and and everyone involved in here. Um, so I'm really really as a coach that means a ton and you want to give everything you can to this organization for that. >> Just to be clear about dealing it talk that this contract situation is causing them to do a holding situation. Are you saying it has nothing to do with that? >> Yeah. Like again it's just injuries for me. I can't speak on those things. >> That's not an injury. I mean that would be a protest of his contract and then the final year. >> Yeah. like I stay out all that stuff. It's above my pay grade. I coach the safeties. I'll keep doing that. Uh let other people handle the other things. I don't get involved with any of those things. >> Um how have your guys and the defense just in general responded to the miles trade? How's morale? What what what's the vibe? >> You know, morale's been great. One, I'll say that. I think the guys have have responded really well. And I think they've responded really well because we got a great player back. Um, you know, to see Jared out there, to know what he's done, you know, to know that the future is still super bright for him and and what he's already done in this league is really special. So, for us, I think the guys are excited about that. I think that gave them a lot of, you know, it it kept morale up and uh and we're excited to add another great player to the room with an awesome mentality. By the way, this guy is, you want to talk about a guy that gets after it and and hates when he's told to like slow down. That's awesome. So, it's been good. And the guys have enjoyed that. >> What you were saying about Emanuel, how obviously you haven't been able to see him on the field as much, but you've been really impressed mentally by what he's been doing in there. Can you elaborate? Are there any examples or something that stood out to you that's impressed you? >> Front of the row, right? His notes and his diligent note takingaking, the amount of extra time he asked for for, you know, our professional or our developmental department, uh, Heidi Saloo's done a great job with him. Like, this guy is super eager for you. He gets in the he gets in here and tries to get all his treatment done so he can go and get extra stuff done wherever he can. So you don't see that with the rookie a lot of times. You got to tell those guys to do that sometimes. This young man is on it, man. So he's done a great job. I think he's been really well coached in college and he's built a really good routine. Uh Jason Kandle's one of the best in the business and you can see the development that man's had in college and you see it in his players and it's really transitioned well to the NFL early. I know I know you haven't seen him on the field a lot here, but coming out of Toledo, do you think early on there's a spot where he fits best? Where he's most comfortable, whether it's, you know, deep center field or close to line of scrimmage? >> You know, obviously at Toledo, that third level stuff was impressive. I mean, the play he makes in Minnesota in the snow, it's phenomenal. His ability, his range, his instincts, uh, his ability just to see the game and really break at the third level is really impressive. Um, but I see a lot more at the second level that we can develop. The arm length, the strength, the uh the ability to play long and, you know, just be such a wimpy like human where he can really create space and and and play, you know, really shorten areas with his length. Uh, is impressive. So, I'm excited to improve that area for him and and grow that area. I think early, you know, maybe, you know, where he's a little bit more comfortable to see things, but the guy has tools to do everything. He can run, he can play man coverage. We just got to keep polishing those things up. >> I apologize for sort of the basic question here, but pass game coord if it's a pass game coordinator. I mean, kind of explain kind of the I don't know if flowchart is the right way, but the the synergy that goes between you and Rudy and Brandon and and and everybody and how that how that all sorts sort of work, >> you You know, at the end of the day, it's just uh it's it's a title that, you know, gives me the responsibility, which I'm very grateful for, to oversee certain things and have a little bit more of a hand in. But I'll say this, that man right there, Coach Lynch, we work side to side, and we've done an amazing job of that for 4 years. That is my brother. We do everything together. Every decision we make is together. Even if we agree, we we agree to disagree, and we go out there and make the best decision possible for our players. and Rudy's been awesome to add to that mix. So for us, it's the same. Like there's not much of a difference in there. We work together. It's, you know, he's yang, I'm yang. And we do a great job of playing off of each other in that. And to be honest with you, we've been doing that for 4 years and that's what, you know, Jim was, you know, relied a lot on us in that space. He'd say, "Hey, if it's the way I want it, you guys go figure it out. We go get it done." And we have and we'll continue to do that. >> Chris Edmonds is a guy that's gotten a lot a lot of reps from the especially, you know, Grant Hend. What have you seen from Penny? What are maybe some teaching points and things you want him to carry on carry over in the training camp? >> Chris has had a phenomenal spring. He really has and I think he's a testament to the development piece of this building. You want to talk about a guy who's really taken advantage of all the different pieces of the development parts of this building over the last few years. He is a he is a walking billboard for that and you can see it out there. His movement, his strength, his conditioning, his mental piece, like the growth that he's had as a player has been awesome. So I think when you have that as another undrafted free agent and you can add that to the deal, you create value for the organization, you create value for the roster, you create value in the room. So done an awesome job of taking advantage of, you know, the question earlier of not having all our guys full go and and some guys take advantage, some don't. He's an example of a guy who has. >> And I know Rudy has said that he really wants to keep like the core of the game intact. Do you think that like especially with his background being defensive passing coordinator, do you think there's some opportunities to incorporate like late rotations and maybe even score too high because you guys >> Yeah, obviously don't want to give away trade secrets. Uh but I'm excited about the things that we've added that that he has brought. Uh really am. Um and he's done a great job of doing that, listening to how we did it and then finding a way to make it melt together, which I think great coordinators do. And I think he's done a great job of that. So, I'm excited about what we have coming. I'm I know you guys will get to see it. You got to wait till after the summer. Uh but I'm excited to where we're headed. I'm excited where we've added and I think it will benefit the room a lot. >> With Hickman, um basically they're in practice and you saw his tender this morning. Um just like what are you looking forward for him this coming season and his role? First off, you know, I'm just extremely excited for him, you know, to sign that deal, to see him go undrafted, to see him start his first game, which was week one versus the Bengals, and play a ton for us to the point to where he just signed this deal. Like, you do that as a that's why you do this as a coach. You do that to see the the growth and development of a player like that. My expectations for him is to take the next step to continue to prove to the entire league why he should have been drafted and why he is one of the best safeties in the league. I want to see him get the ball and be more, you know, and and have a more opportunities to be ball productive. I want to see him continue to grow in the communication piece. He's he's got to orchestrate the thing and I want to see him continue to grow in that area. And then the next piece, which we've talked about, is just being a really good all-around safety, not just a free safety that was asked earlier, a second level guy who can play in the box and be he's got 33 inch arms. So, I want to see him grow as a allaround safety, you know, this year, which I think he's done a great job of applying this to spring. >> You guys have a great summer. See you guys. >> Thank you. >> Yep.

title: Bradley Chubb Talks About Season Goals At Minicamp | Buffalo Bills
text: super blessed to have, you know, just how God's blessed me, uh my family, my new found wife, you know what I mean? All the things that uh you know, just been having to be great for me this off season. >> How big a part of coming here is a chance to win? >> It's a huge part, man. It's a huge part. And um outside looking in, it's always like damn, the Bills always had that formula. They know how to win. They know how to finish out those close games. And being around here, you see why, you know what I mean? You see the people in the locker room. You see the the support staff that that helps everybody, you know, keep the main thing the main thing. And so, being a part of it like on the inside now is really dope to see. And I'm hoping we can continue to build on that. >> You haven't gotten a chance to play in a ton of playoff games. Like how much does that hunger >> One game. >> grow as you as you get older? Yeah, it was just it was here, right? >> here. Yeah, yeah, yeah. My hunger is is through the roof, man. That's top of the team. That's like my biggest goal, man, is to win games. And that's what you, you know, in the league, man, you start off young. So, that first you want to get your feet under you, make a name for yourself. Then you want to get paid. And then like the championship stuff, you know, comes down the line. But I've been in that mindset for a while. Just hasn't happened for me, unfortunately. But, you know, that's why I'm here now for it, you know. And not making no promises that we're going to win the Super Bowl. But, everybody's in the right alignment. Everybody's doing the things that we know we can do. That's that's going to be the you know, that's the end goal. And that's what I'm shooting for every day. >> Have you been to this like I know a lot of guys go to the Super Bowl for media stuff. >> I went last year. Yeah, I went last year. I was yeah, I was the Dolphins Walter Payton >> Okay, yep. >> Player of the Year nominee. And I went That was my first time seeing the atmosphere, seeing the you know, the flyover, the the national anthem, the start of the game. Like all the stuff they did, it just like lit a fire in me, honestly. And it's crazy cuz it's crazy how life works. I was sitting right next to Deion the whole time. You know, we talking, chopping it up the whole game. So, it's funny how how how life works like that. And now I'm back up here, you know. So, uh you know, that's the that's the goal, though. Seeing that and and you know, being around that, I know what to what to expect, you know what I mean? So, that's going That's been in in mind ever since then. And that's what I'm shooting for. >> Brother, you talk about wanting to win a championship with this team. And so many guys in this locker room obviously want that too. So it's just what do you think though? You mean you've been in this league long enough. What does it take that little minute detail that it takes for a team to finally get over that hump? >> I feel like it's about hitting the stride at the right time, you know. Right now we in our season program building, you know, having the building blocks putting it in the in the right direction. Um but you know, you don't want to get too far ahead of yourself and think, oh, week 12 we got to make sure we're at this point, you know what I mean? It's just about you know, hitting the groove at the right time and being a team, forming and having those, you know, those uh adverse situations that you got to grow from and getting past those and and you know, making it happen. And another thing too, I see past couple years defense has been the main thing, you know, and we did a lot of revamping on the defense this year. So I'm excited to see how we all come together. >> What's it been like working with Greg just opposite edge of you? >> It's been great, man. It's been great. Um he's a great guy. Just been around him, you know, talking life, talking ball with him. He's he's to play with his off season down in Florida, too. So we're going to be have a chance to connect in that sense, but yeah, he's a good dude, man. Everybody in the outside linebacker room has been, like I said, very welcoming, very arms open to receptive to everything I'm telling them. I'm receptive to everything they're telling me about what they see and stuff like that. So it's been a it's been a great working environment for sure. >> Has the transition to this defense been pretty easy for you like >> Yeah, honestly, it's kind of what I've been in my whole career. When I first got into the league, I was in a version of this defense with Vance Joseph, where coach Leonard came from. So it's kind of like a a lot of things re-hashing, but a lot of the techniques and stuff are the same thing I've been doing for a while. >> Does it help you find your leadership voice when it's like you have the experience in the defense? Maybe you can naturally like help some guys out and stuff like that. >> Yeah, that helps for sure. Being able to, you know, kind of give a eight-year perspective of what I've seen in the in the scheme, for sure. So yeah, guys have questions, I'm trying to be the first one there to answer for them. Um and like I said, we're always bouncing ideas off each other, too. So that's been dope. >> Knowing that you know, you've just been in this system for before, what does it take to be a successful outside linebacker? >> Aggressiveness, I would say. You know, not thinking not not thinking, but not like having those thoughts weigh you down. Just playing fast, playing physical, getting off the ball, putting you know, fear in the tackles feet in both the run and the pass, you know what I mean? And if you got guys who's been in in this defense in the past like Nick Perry know Jonathan Cooper, they do the same things, you know, they just get off the ball and and questions later, you know? So, that's what our main emphasis for us has been and I feel like that's what we got to do for this defense to really amplify.

title: T.J. Sanders On Team's Work During Minicamp | Buffalo Bills
text: How did that week go coming into a break now? Kind of just thoughts on that and what's next for you for the six-week break you got? >> Uh you know, it went good. Uh you know, every day was a work day for us. Feel like we got better as a group, as individuals as well. You know, this next six weeks is about keeping that up. >> What's it been like just, you know, now getting ready for this break, but you've got a pretty good, you know, baseline of Jim's defense? Just how do you think guys are responding to it and are you noticing, you know, a little bit of that want to get after the quarterback mentality? >> Yeah, uh I feel like guys are embracing it. Um me and me included. Um just like knowing what Jim wants out of us, uh out of certain calls, and you know, being able to go put that on the field. >> So many guys have talked about like they could feel like they're playing more free with Jim's defense. Would you say that's kind of how you feel, too? >> Yeah, I agree. I'm also one of the guys that said that, you know, feel like I got you know, a lot more freedom to kind of, you know, be the player that I know I am. >> Uh Bradley Chubb, what have you just learned a little bit about him getting to work with a guy like that on the edge? >> Uh great guy, you know, on and off the field. title: Sean Rhyan 1-on-1: 'Part of the reason they paid me was to not change'
text: When you look in the mirror now, are you seeing a center now? >> Yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Definitely. Um especially after the you know last year and and you know what unfolded and you know in this off season all of that, yeah. Definitely center. >> Uh and besides seeing that, like could you talk about your comfort level at the position because uh there's a lot that goes into it, you know, you're you know, everybody makes calls but you're making a lot of them. >> Yeah. >> And you got the shotgun snap and you got you know, there's just a lot of stuff going on. >> Your comfort level with the position now. Could you talk about that? >> Uh every day I'm getting more comfortable. Um I'm not going to say I'm not comfortable there, you know, cuz we had you know, quite a bit going last year but uh every day is just getting better, you know, feeling it, uh becoming second nature, you know, trying to build that uh uh unknown like unspoken communication with the guys over there on the line. So, yeah, every day getting more and more comfortable. >> Would you say now that you've been through it, it's something you you know, that we can talk about it, we can do it on the board and you can do it sometimes but you got to actually do it and own it to really get comfortable? >> Yeah. I mean you like you said, you could you know, draw it on the board and you know, say that's what you're going to do but until you're doing it out there on the field and really you know, executing to a high level, uh it's hard to say that you're comfortable at it, you know, so uh I'm sure with more games coming up and and this year it'll it'll flow together. >> Now, it was certainly the fact that gave you a vote of confidence at the position with your extension and all that good stuff. Uh like does that you know, after getting that, does it change anything or how do you approach that? I mean you know what I mean? >> Yeah, yeah. >> I mean I'll tell you what, they pay centers a lot better now. >> [laughter] >> I think I think part of the reason they paid me is to not change. You know, keep the same work ethic, the same uh you know, just being the same guy every day I think is what um they paid me for. So, I'm going to try to do that and you know, I'm obviously trying to evolve as, you know, a vet and a leader now, too. So, um building my skills as a leader I think is what I've been doing through OTAs, you know, asking Aaron about, you know, certain things, picking things off him and whatnot. Um but yeah. Yeah. >> One One last thing for you. I I I personally you bring a physicality to the position. And and you got the body that it matters. Like is that would you say that's an important part of your game, the physical the physicality of it? >> I think so. I don't want to say I'm a huge center, but I I feel like I'm a little bit bigger than than the quote-unquote, you know, center, normal center, but I think playing physical is part of my game and I think it's becoming part of everyone else's game as well. Aaron plays physical, J'Marr plays physical, AB plays physical, ZT, everyone's playing physical. So, I think I like to play physical, they like to play physical, you know, it's going to be a a physical year. >> Yeah. Yeah. It's going to be uh part of part of it. Yeah.

title: Packers Unscripted: Minicamp musings (but we digress)
text: [music] Hi everybody. Welcome to another edition of Packers Unscripted from Packers.com. But with regard to mini camp, a lot to cover here. And it starts with the media session from Packers tight end Tucker Craft after Wednesday's practice. And uh there's a story on Packers.com if you want to check it out. I wrote that, posted it this morning. Um, the biggest thing I took away from listening to Tucker Craft is um, a not only how confident he is that he can be full go, no limitations come week one, but he is just as confident, if not more so, that he will not only be the same player when he comes back, but an even better one. >> Yeah, it was great listening to Tuck. Uh, and it's been a minute since uh, our last update with him. Obviously, he held court at the end of the season, too. But now being, you know, four months further along in this process with the ACL, um it there's so many parallels I thought as I was listening to him between his discussion and the discussion we had a week earlier with Micah Parsons and just that the maturity and the understanding of he's by all accounts, by every measure, Tucker Craft is ahead of schedule, way ahead of schedule. Um, but as he said when he was asked about it, it's still very realistic for him to start training camp on the pup list. Uh, the main reason for that being that once you're back, you know, either you're on pup or you're not, right? So, it's like once you're back, you can't go backwards. Now, now you got to go forward. So, I think the Packers are going to be smart with him, have a plan for him throughout training camp with the end goal being week one, regular season opener, being on no pitch count, number 85, being number 85. This is a critical year for Tucker Craft, not just because of the contract extension, which he also touched on during the discussion, >> but to show that he is still that guy he was before the injury. And that guy in his estimation was one of the best all-around tight ends in the National Football League. And seeing him after this little pit stop, I think you would call it get back to form. He said he last week was running 21 and a half miles an hour on the treadmill. I mean, this guy has put every ounce of sweat in his off season and in his rehab to getting back on the field and being better than ever. >> Yeah. And [clears throat] it does sound like or he made it sound like he does expect to start training camp on PUP. He doesn't expect to be ready for day one of training camp. I think that's probably part of the ninemonth rule that Micah Parsons was talking about with regard to his recovery. But the fact that he said not only week one, but the whole no pitch count thing, like no no limitations. I think uh um that uh um that definitely caught everybody's ear. It was interesting because um in the midst of, you know, all the reporters being around him, I just I asked him a very quick question about what the hardest part of the process was. and he actually went back and just talked about how just not being out there on the field, you know, being able to be the guy, be the leader in the locker room and everything because he wasn't a part of things like that was the hardest part. It wasn't it's hasn't been about the rehab part. That hasn't been the hardest part for him. So, he put the most difficult part behind him several months ago. But it was funny because then I'm thinking in my mind of, you know, another question I wanted to ask him because he was on pace to have the best season ever by a Packers tight end based on catches, yards, touchdowns, and all that. He was on pace midway through the year to to shatter all those marks. But then in the midst of the conversation, he started talking about how, you know, he wants to, expects to is going to continue his quest to be the best tight end in the NFL. And then I realized the question I wanted to ask him about, you know, do you think that best season for a Packers tight end in history is still in your horizon? I realized it was sort of a dumb question. So, I didn't even ask it because >> um it's the way he was sounding. It's he he he he just expects to pick up exactly where he left off, if not be even better. And whatever the best statistical season for a Packers tight end in history is going to be, he absolutely plans on being the guy to do that. So, I kind of just kept my mouth shut because I didn't want to get that Tucker Craft glare of like, what are you asking me, bro? you know, like um but uh um it's it's easy to forget in some ways just how good an individual season he was having last year. And that's aside from everything he means in the locker room as a leader and and what he means to his teammates >> um off the field and all that. And uh I mean I I can't wait to see him back out there doing his thing. >> Yeah. and and he had mentioned that too and he was looking at um last year and kind of in the the rearview mirror of where he was. I mean the way he leads is what he does on the field, right? It it's the way he plays the tight end position.
