text: feel like we always ask rookies this, but coming in in year two, how much different is it in this camp for you now having the season under your belt? >> Uh, I feel way better. I don't feel as nervous. Um, so I'm playing faster. Uh, yeah, I've learned I learned a lot last year, so just trying to use that to build on this year and, you know, get better. >> Not having pads on. Obviously, that's how you guys make a living. But what did you learn last year that's already helping you in this setting right now in OTAAS? >> Uh, just how the NFL is played. like it's a lot different than college. Uh players are way better, you know, schemes are way better. Um so just having a year under my belt, I feel like I'm just playing faster and more fluid. >> Any kind of big goals for you this off season, setting yourself up for success going into year two? >> Uh probably shed a little bit more weight. Um like I said, just playbook, you know, being a better teammate. Um that's probably it. >> What about your position? Do you expect that to maybe expand a little bit in terms of moving up and down the line a little bit? >> Yeah, I think I'll be playing some nose this year and some three tech, but we'll see. >> Okay. >> What is it about the edges that have been added to this room? Kelvin was telling us all the length that he sees around now and how much the team went out and addressed it. Do you see a lot different options around you edges guys and how much different their bodies look? >> Oh yeah, we did bring in a bunch of like long arm like guys. So, I mean, I think it'll help. We'll see. I don't I don't know. >> What's the talk been like between you and Derek and another Michigan guy in that room? >> Uh, you know, we have our, you know, conversations about the game. Obviously, I troll him. He trolls me, but, you know, he's a good dude. He's a great player and he'll help us. >> Am closer to 100% this year. I know DJ was a big leader in that defensive tackle room, but how much have you looked to Ale over this off season to to kind of pick up more more tips on how to play the positions? >> True. So I talk to Alem every day about something with football. So last year it was DJ and Alem. Now it's Alem. So I mean Alem helps me whenever I need help and he's been that great leader for me going into year two. >> What's it like having rookies look at you? It's kind of like a hey where do we go? Where do we go get food? How do we work around this building? Do you realize you're putting on a veteran hat here in year two? >> Uh I don't know if it's that but you know I I help when I can. It's kind of weird being like a having been a rookie last year, you know, looking around for everything. and now I'm helping people. It is kind of weird, but you know, I'm all for it. >> Just speak to your your mindset heading into this year being healthy. You already you played last year. You started so well and then obviously had the hamstring injury. Such a tough injury to come back from and just having to deal with that. Just what's it like to be uh 100% healthy? Just your mindset heading into year two here? >> Yeah, that's a great question. I would say well the main goal for me is just to stay healthy. I think that's like really important and that's just, you know, doing my system, just hydrating, getting the right amount of sleep, just doing everything I can control. And, um, yeah, this offseason I did a lot as far as like treatment regarding the hamstring just to get back to where I needed to be. >> Um, I got stem cells. I went to Panama, got some stem cells, and was just rehabbing during the offseason and training. And um it feels good, but it's something that you got to keep, you know, continuing to like, you know, work out and rehab. >> Considering that start that you had last year, I mean, you're trying to plow through and get back. How frustrating was it going through the injury you went through? >> Man, it was tough. It was tough. It was It was tough. I'm not going to lie, just with the severity of the strain. It was a bad strain. Um I thought that I initially needed surgery, but yeah, it's football. Like, nobody cares. So, I mean, it it was tough rehabbing. like I had to teach myself how to walk, how to jog, sprint again, and then going back to playing football was it was a tough task, but there's no excuses. Like when you're out there, you're out there. So, I'm definitely looking forward to um getting back healthy and balling out and doing what I was doing before the injury. >> How were you feeling exactly when you were out there like after coming back from the injury? Like, what percentage were you and then I guess how does that compare to how you feel now? >> Well, the rehab team here, they did a great job. Like, it wasn't like I was going out there and I couldn't run. It was just more so like when I was watching the tape and watching how I was covering guys before the injury, I was just more stickier and I had that that burst that I'm accustomed to having. And just with watching, you know, later in the season, other games, it was like same thing, same technique, but guys were just running by me. So, it just didn't have that that extra gear. So, it was definitely humbling and I definitely had to alter like some of the some of the ways that I had to play just to stay on top. >> Sure. >> Did you feel like you have that burst back now? >> Yeah, it's it's definitely there now. What about the just a second year in chef's system and what does that do for a player just the comfort level of maybe not having to think as much as as you had last year just be able to play? >> Yeah, I definitely feel much more comfortable in the system. I would say it's really I'm really happy to be here during OTAAS just because we have new safeties. So just getting the looks with them and also Roger our nickel. So just they're new guys so they're learning a whole new system. So just getting the reps with them and understanding how they play is very important instead of me just coming to training camp and not knowing how everyone plays. >> How long were you in Panama last season? >> Um just one week. >> Just one week. >> Yeah. >> Where do you get the idea of that stem cell research stuff? Was there a player or >> Yeah. Um Fred Warner actually I want to say two years ago. Me and Fred are good friends. We both got drafted together in San Francisco. He told me about stem cells. So, I've been going there for not only my Hemi from last year, but I I get a couple things done while I'm down there. >> With those new faces and a lot of talk about the competition in the secondary that's been ramped up. What do you think camp is going to mini camp, but also training camp is going to be like different maybe than last year? >> Um, coaches talk about it a lot. I think it's going to be much more competitive. Like, it's like not a lot of solidified spots. So, it's just going to bring bring more competition every day, which is I think good for the betterment of everybody. Do you feel that already just in the rooms and out here? I mean, obviously it's not real. >> Yeah, I would say like, you know, they say in OTAAS, you don't lose your job, but I I feel like every day you're being evaluated and, you know, you got to put your best foot forward with every practice you get. >> A lot of questions about the safeties, especially with Bryant and Kirby's injuries. Do you feel like >> there's enough depth on this team for you guys to answer those questions in your own way? >> I believe so. like we got we got a lot of guys. They brought a lot of guys in. Um Chuck Clark, I think he's been doing a great job with the role they've asked him to play at safety. Um you know, he's in year 10, so he's been around a lot of football, and you could tell just cuz he just understands it. Izzy, he's still learning, but he's super athletic. Um he could range around the field. He does good um down in the box, so he he fills that role, I believe. And Roger, he's learning a lot at nickel right now. And it's a lot because we put a lot on our nickels, but he's learning and, you know, he's trying to understand it the best to his abilities and he's doing a great job, too. >> Yeah, he's just a locked in dude. He just he just takes his business serious like Yeah, I'll just leave it at that. I'll just leave it at that. >> What's been chef's message to you guys? >> The messages has been really like when we get back to training camp, we're not starting back over. I think that's important because we put all the installs in during OTAAS. And even though in training camp, we're going to reinstall those installs, but we're not going to be well, they're they don't want to coach like the basics. They want us to already come in and know that with the five weeks we get off. >> How have you kind of seen him develop coming into his second year? What do you see? How have you seen him? Is he communicating any differently as obviously kind of dropping the ball? Um, I mean, I thought he did a great job last year, especially with all the injuries, especially in the back end, but I would say Coach Shep seems um, a little more poised this year compared to last year, just as far as just like, you know, correcting people. Like, I think he's just more poised about it and I think he's explaining things even better than he did last year. >> Chef's always called you that fourth starter, you know, for ever since you've really been here. Play a ton as a rookie. What is it like going into a season as the actual, you know, kind of starter? At least you're getting first team reps and you have a chance for that role. >> Yeah, I mean really no different. I mean, chef's always preached about competition. So, it's one of those things. You come back to camp getting ready for competition and best best guy would play. When >> you knew you had a chance to play, you know, somebody that will spot. What was the focus for you this off season? What was your game maybe related to that position in particular that you know, hey, I got to maybe get a little better year. I got to work on this. >> It was never to play big. It was always just about getting healthy. coming back from injury, getting healthy, you know, coming from last season wasn't, you know, I didn't feel like my best like what I used to feel like. So, it's one of those things going in the offseason, fresh mindset, clear mindset, and uh get uh getting back right. I'll ask kind of the same question just maybe a different way. Just to be here and to see more opportunity in front of you for more playing time. Do you feel different walking into this training camp in July coming up here than than you have in previous years? >> Uh other than obviously feeling healthy, no, I really don't. I mean, it's one of those things where, like I said, every every year I come in, it's always competition. So, um, I take it as it comes and it's one of those things where, like I said, it's competition all around and Shep's always preach that in the defensive meeting room. So, uh, you guys are going to throw us out there, give us opportunities, and you go out there, have a chance to make plays. >> Looks like just throughout defense, it seems like there's a ton of compos competition at a ton of spots. Do you get that kind of vibe, too, all >> that? Yeah, I mean it it brings the level uh of play up for sure and it's one of those things where like you know those guys are going to stand out uh to the competition. So like I said, Chef and all the coaches preach it all the time about the level of competition and uh training camp's going to it's going to be a great one this year. >> What's your level of hunger given that you know you haven't necessarily been like full-time start since that preseason obviously putting in a lot of work in special teams. How how hungry have you been to get out there and play on defense? >> Uh always hungry. You know, it's one of those things where, like I said, you get the opportunity, you got to go out there and showcase, you know, my talents again. So, it's one of those things where, like I said, coming into this year, it's kind of refresh and going back in there like like I'm a rookie again. So, that's the mindset you got to have and you just got to keep going. >> Year two with Shep running the defense. Just how you see him, his ability to communicate with you guys and >> uh he he they did a a good job at doing like, you know, self scout. So, it's one of those things where like, you know, what worked well last year and what didn't. So, uh, he's very, uh, knowledgeable coach like that and he's always implementing on us and teaching us all the little details in and out of like offense and not just defense. So, it's, uh, it's, uh, he's awesome DC to have and, you know, excited to play for him again. >> Healthwise, what was something that was maybe missing towards the end of last year when you came back versus how you feel now? >> Yeah, I mean, it's just one of those things I was dealing with some stiffness, you know, trying to get do some scar tissue and all that and, you know, getting that mental uh, strength back. So, it's one of those things where like this year like I feel 10 times better night and day. So, it's uh like I said, last season last season and this year, you know, I'm excited to come in healthy. >> Did it feel like it was more of a mental thing or were there some physicalations? >> Um, could be a little bit of both. So, it's one of those things where I've never had to deal with injury. So, it's like, you know, something new for me. So, had to kind of just jump over that bridge and, you know, water under the bridge now.

title: Kelvin Sheppard Media Availability | June 4, 2026
text: I know it's early. One of the rooms that you guys revamped quite a bit was was that edge rusher room. You got to give Aiden, you know, some some help there. I'm just curious understanding no pads yet, but just maybe just first impressions of what you like from that room and and and maybe the mix that you got there. >> Absolutely. Well, on the first look at it, it's like, oh, it's changed over there. And that corner you look there an individual, it's a lot of big, long, tall the biggest thing that stand out to me is length. That's something that we kind of attacked and then we saw that we needed and like always, you know, we mentioned it and the front office did a great job trying to go out and kind of attain and attract some of the, you know, boring what we could do some of the top guys per what we were looking for and I thought they did a great job. And you said something that's kind of it is a good mix and blend. You have some long, you have some you have some more shorter, powerful, so to say, type players. So, the first thing I think it's going to be a lot of competition come training camp with that unit. I mean, it's six, seven guys right now I'm looking at and they all look like they can play and have potential. It's just a matter of when the pads come on and kind of how does that look. >> Just two little follow-ups on that. Where did the length, not having the length hurt you if anywhere last year? Like what did you need that to upgrade that for? And then second, Dan just mentioned in passing Anthony Lucas, you know, undrafted guy, but is he is he someone that's caught your eye? >> Absolutely. Look, and that's why I say six, seven. You go in there, we know the obvious. The guys kind of when the banner goes across ESPN, DJ Wonnum signed, DJ Wonnum Lions drafted Derrick Moore, former first-rounder Peyton Turner, but the guys they may not know is guy like I met, spent last year on practice squad. He's looking to make a push to this roster. Guy like Anthony Lucas. And you know, you turn on his college tape. I turned on his junior film at USC and unfortunately it was against LSU and he was a game wrecker. He He legitimately and if people go back, those two tackles they played at LSU that year, uh they both one was the number four pick and the other one in the third round. Those were some pretty good players. Uh and he wrecked that game. So, as a guy I had my radar up on like how did we get this guy and draft it? Uh so, we're very excited. Uh we're very excited for that group. Uh but when it comes to the length, I heard you ask that question. Just that's what you look for on the edges nowadays, especially what complements the werewolf that we have. You know, what what does that look like? Um a lot of guys want this juiced-up speedball type player, but does that truly complement what that player does well? And that's something that we had to sit back as a staff, uh as a front office and look at. Um and I think we all are on the same page as far as what we're looking for to complement that player. >> Eric Armstead some high praise for Jimmy Roloder in the IQ standpoint, just the way he's picking things up so quickly. It's a guy that didn't see, you know, a ton of snaps during his college career. What What do you think he's been able to kind of pick up what you're laying down so so quickly? >> Oh, it starts with Shawn Dean and Hamilton, uh linebacker coach that I feel is one of the best in the league when it comes to developing. When people ask me what do I look for in a coach? It's a teacher and and more importantly it's a guy that can develop and pull the most out of his guys. Um and and um and Ham does that each and every day. Pours into these players and they feel it. Uh and then when it comes to Jimmy it means something to him to be honest and to play linebacker and safety in this system, especially where we've taken it now. Uh it takes a lot. Uh it takes mental capacity uh and he has it. Um he still has a lot of ways to grow. Like this isn't a guy we're looking to go out and call the defense tomorrow, but his trajectory and where we see things going for him is definitely on the upswing. >> How confident are you he is going to leave and is going to be back to where he was two years ago? >> Um as confident as I've ever been. Uh, and what builds confidence is like a lot of people say how why? Why are you confident? You haven't played a game. It's demonstrated ability. Uh, last year there were things on tape that clearly showed us in his mind. It wasn't physical. And even Alim addressed it and that's the biggest thing. When you have players that attack you before you do as a coach, first thing he says is I got to be better for you, Ship. I said I got to be better for you. And when you got players that see it like that and they live in reality and not this realm of oh, I I should have had 20 sacks last year. Really? Let's turn the tape on and what does that say? And Alim's like I didn't play up to par, but it had nothing to do with physical capabilities. He he he was back, but it's a mental thing. It's a mental gap between I'm not hurt anymore and I could cut it [clears throat] loose. Um, and he's closed that gap and we see the Mac that we all know right now out on the grass. But again, it's spring. We need to see what this looks like in training camp. >> I want to ask you about uh, Thomas Harper. He gave you nine starts last year. What What was your assessment of how he was able to step up and then what is your um, confidence in his ability if he has to play another big role for you this year? >> Yeah, that's actually another position. I know we talked about the D-line, but another position that the front office did a good job addressing with the uncertainty as the safety spot. Uh, we bringing guys in that's had time on task so to say and has played a lot of ball in this league. Uh, Thomas Harper, I don't know if people are aware of this, but last year was his first time truly playing safety. He played nickel in Las Vegas for the Raiders. He was more of a nickel corner hybrid type player and never had fully poured into the safety spot. And that's not easy to do in the NFL. You get to this level because it's repetition. It's It's It's a lot of second nature things that take place. Um, instincts kick in and those are things where you saw him getting better through the course of the year and he played a lot of good quality football. Those were quality snaps he were able to log. Uh but we do feel he's continuing to grow, he's continuing to get better, and he's a player that's going to push that unit to kind of be in that lineup. >> What did you see from him to make you think he could play safety? >> Uh the range of the player. That's That's kind of his superpower. When you talk about an angel in the outfield, what did What is the superpower that player? It's two things, range and then the ability to what we call eraser tackle. That's when the ball pops. An NFL the guy in the deep, he better be able to do those two things, have range and instincts, and then when the ball pops, get the ball on the ground. And again, why do I believe it? Cuz demonstrated ability. The ball popped on him a few times last year, he got it on the ground. He showed range. Now it's about Now let's take that range and let's tick it up a bit and let's go make a play on the ball versus being close. And that's the leap that we all have to take as a team right now. We're not in this to be close, we're in this to go do it, and that starts players, that starts per play, per game, so on and so forth. >> And then the you know, branching, Kirby being out, and then also the departure of Alex, does that change your thinking as far as like how how much you devote resources to the to the secondary, maybe structure the defense where it leans more towards pass coverage? >> No, again, we have a system and we have something that we know who we are here. Now, does that alter week to week? Yeah, per game plan. Does that alter per things you put in? Listen, listen, now make no mistake, I'm not going to shy away from this. Those are two all-pro caliber players. I don't care what position they play. When you go from all-pro to anybody, there's some type of change that has to take place. And it's my job, whether I have those two guys or whether I have X, Y, and Z, to make sure I'm putting those players in the best position and putting my pride aside and what I want to be. I know who we are, but also understanding what do these players do well and trying to mesh that and how does that look? So, that's kind of the process that we've been afforded right now with those two guys not being out there. We've gone through weeks of that process so far and we seeing it and we're liking where we at right now. So, I'm not saying necessarily there's a schematic overhaul whether we have those players or not. That's not the case. Again, the front office did a tremendous job bringing in guy like Chuck Clark, 10th-year guy. He's played a lot of football in this league. We got a guy like Avonte Maddox back, 9th-10th year guy. Played a lot of ball in this league. A guy like Christian Izien that we've played against the last 3 years, logged a lot of snaps at multiple positions, but we've been dousing him at the safety spot. And then bringing back a guy like Thomas Harper. And then you have Lawrence Strickland. You have Dane Jackson, a guy that got hurt early in the process last year who was showing some promise. So, it's a lot of guys in that room where we don't know what's that's going to look like. I have no idea, but whoever the two guys are, they're going to be able to operate well within what we do as a defense here. >> Just last, does the nickel position take on more importance though? I mean, the nickel corner position uh based on just just that fact. When you have more time on task with something or hopefully, so I say hopefully you're not going backwards, you're going forward in life. But that's just natural. With time on task, again, I I told the players today and D, that's why we practice, guys. Repetition, it becomes muscle memory. Now, I've gone through a season where I I've had to adapt, I've had to adjust. I saw where things might have should have went one way and it didn't go that way. Well, why? And identifying that. So now the next time that exact same circumstance comes up, oh yeah, guys, we talked about that last year. This is what we're going to do. This is how we're going to attack that. There's conversations being had right now in the spring because of what they've presented offensively. So just solutions. That's when Dan sits in with us, he's like, "I'm loving this because what I hear is problem solvers." And that's why I love my staff. And I live and die by those guys because I've yet to hear a guy say, "Well, we don't have those safeties. What are we going to do?" Or "Oh, that was a hard play." Life is hard. That's why you're tasked with these jobs and responsibilities. It's our jobs as coaches and leaders to figure it out and make it easy on the players. They got to go out there and perform. >> The week-to-week matches, when we talked to you back in in Indy, you said you wanted to be more versatile. That was a big thing for the defense just to match up week-to-week if you guys do something different. Getting a look at these guys now, do you feel like you're in a better place to be a little bit more versatile just from what you seen early on? >> Absolutely. I mean, you just look at the secondary unit in totality. There's about seven, eight guys. I mean, you throw Abney in there that we drafted who's played, I mean, a lot of snaps. And there's a lot of versatility we feel like within that group. There's guys that versus will that be college, going back to college or the NFL, they spent time in the slot, they spent time outside. There's some swing players that spent time at safety like Nezihian. He came over here and said, "What you guys need me to play?" I said, "I might need you to learn two spots." He's like, "Oh, that'll be one less than I had in Tampa cuz I had to know three." He He [laughter] said so. Like, being able to have guys that's used to that and used to adapting cuz that's You asked me what I learned and why am I more comfortable. The adaptability, the adaptability rate that you have as a coach and a player in this league is vital because things are going to change. We're going to have set plans when we go into into week one. And probably by the second quarter of the Saints game, something's going to be different than what we thought it was going to be. And in that moment, who are you? And that's what we're going through right now. >> Coach, what are some of the main takeaways from here? What are some of the main takeaways from here? >> you Kaden and Dave. >> What are some of the main takeaways from your offseason deep dive of the defense and how have you seen maybe some of those changes playing out so far in the offseason? >> Oh, I mean, you know, there was a lot of takeaways. We've been at this thing for months now. And when I tell you no stone unturned, there was no stone unturned. But just identifying the whys behind why things happened. Kaden, like to tell you the truth, why did it happen? We know it happened. Let's not sit in here and go, "Gave up 105 explosives." Who Or whose fault what? No. Why did it happen? So, then these last eight weeks with these players, we've been able to come in and explain to them the why behind it. We're not pointing a finger at you, but you need to understand there was either a lack of understanding, a lack of detail, or the So, coach to player, player to player, or something got off. Because this shouldn't be happening. We talked about the situation and identifying it and everybody taking ownership within that. And then as far as like schematically, we did see room for certain things we do. Like we know here we want to be a man team and we want to play man. But is that the best thing to do in that situation or that week? Whether that be complimentary football of what the offense is doing or whether that be a matchup situation. And just being able, like I said, to adapt in those moments and not being hard-headed and stubborn. Yeah, we have principles and we not moving off those, but again, adapting and adjusting within that. >> I just want to go back to Chuck Clark for a quick second. He was a pretty good player on some pretty good defenses, you know, early in his career. Is he just from what you've seen of him of late, has he changed his game at all? How is he What can he add to the defense? >> What I'll say right now, Chuck Clark is a man of man. He is a man, a grown man. Like he walks in the room and if you guys spend any time with him, you'll know that. I've never seen him smile. And that's not because he's a bad guy or nothing. Like I talked to him on the phone, I'm like, "Oh, great family man. We just going to be a good" He came in the room, "Yes, sir. I'm not supposed to do No. No." Like because this means something to him and it's why he's played 10 years in this league. The amount of leadership he's naturally grown into. When Chuck's on the field, you know where the safety is. You know what the check is. You know what the communication is. And that's vital and important. You talk about explosive plays, well, that's the number one component to limiting those. Making sure we're all on the same page. And that's something, take ability aside, Chuck Clark on the field is rarely to never a mistake or Emmy with the back end. And that's because everybody knows who in charge because he makes it known. So, that's the first word I would say, leader, leader, leader. When it comes to to the athletic ability, can he still do certain things? That's still yet to be seen in training camp will allow us that those four to five week period to see what he's still capable of doing. But from everything I've seen so far, this is the player I saw on tape previous to his career, but more importantly the leadership has been outstanding from that player.

title: Klint Kubiak Recaps Minicamp: ‘We’re an Improved Team'
text: Clint, you watch Fernando like I like your style. Get rolling. Let's do it. >> When you watch Fernando, at least your opinion is far more valuable than mine, but it certainly looks as if he's getting extremely more comfortable under center. Is this one of those situations where just because a guy wasn't asked to do something doesn't mean he can't? >> Uh, yeah, he's he's working his tail off. He's he's gotten a ton better. um putting the work in. You know, I think uh it is it is an adjustment, but with anyone um coming into the league, you got to put the work into it, and he's done that. Um we're going to ask him to play under center, we're going to ask him play in the gun, we're asking the pistol, all of our quarterbacks, and that's not just us. That's a leaguewide thing. But, uh the things we've asked him to improve on, he's been diligent at. >> How much urgency is there to get his deal done? >> Uh I'll let Spy handle that. You know, I'll just keep coaching him. Uh Clint, uh in regards to Nico Deans, his absence remaining in mini camp for practice. Is that injury related? >> Yeah, Nico's been here every day. He didn't practice. Uh but you know, all injuries and things like that, you know, I don't want to talk about this time of year. We just want to get all our guys healthy to training camp. That's really the most important thing. >> Jer kind of fit into that category in terms of, you know, just just managing it right now and and getting him to training camp. >> Absolutely. and uh you know you know he's done a great job and we're asking him to spend a lot of time with with AG just to get him ready so that when we put him out there uh come training camp we've have 100% confidence in him and and him the same way. But uh really excited about seeing him practice, you know, come training camp. >> Have his absences kind of just been a part of the plan working with with AG kind of going forward? >> It has. Yeah, AG has got a great plan with our medical staff and we're bringing them along slowly. >> You are not a person given to hyperbole. So, is this team where you thought they would be after mandatory mini camp? A little ahead, a little behind. What is your thoughts and assessment? >> We're an improved team. Our guys, our guys have taken the coaching, you know, they're doing everything we ask them to do. I definitely see an improvement from where we started. And, uh, you know, this time of year, you can kind of get lulled to sleep when the pads aren't on. So, you know, what team that we're going to become, we'll find out, you know, come training camp, we put pads on. There's so many guys that are maybe doing great right now that will disappear, you know, come the fall. There's so many guys that you maybe not notice as much, but all of a sudden, you know, whether it's a running back or an offensive lineman or defensive lineman, now that guy really shows his value. Um, so you get what you can out of this time of year, and then the real evaluation comes, you know, with those 11 practices before we play that first, uh, preseason game. >> You have a you have a recent history of, you know, coming into a situation and having to lay down the groundwork, you know, uh, brand new, the Saints, and then last year with the Seattle Seahawks. Does that help you u in terms of marking the progress kind of knowing where you need to be at this time of year and not getting too far out ahead of yourself? >> Yeah, absolutely. You know, being being a part of many year ones, uh you you learn from your mistakes, you learn what works, uh how to best bring the players along, how not to load them up too much and kind of give them things uh in the install peace meal. And then there's days where you go out there and just stress the heck out of them mentally and see what they can retain. Um but I think it kind of goes back to the people that you're around. And I've been lucky in those two spots uh to be around some some other coaches, some familiarity where you don't have to spend that much time with the offensive line with the with the quarterbacks with guys like Rick and Andrew. So really blessed to have them, you know, on our staff and allows me to go and spend time with other parts of the team. >> Obviously through most the offseason the team didn't have the shield on their helmets and you said that they had to earn that shield and for mini camp they had the shield. um what did they do to to to earn it and did you say anything to them when that happened? >> I just think we knew from the start that uh we were all we were all just, you know, trying to do our part to make the Raiders better and to earn earn the shield and and like I said before, our guys have really worked their tail off and what we've asked them to do as coaches has been a lot this time of year and uh they've bought in and they're working their tail off. So, I thought they they definitely earned that thing. But that's a that's an everyday thing, you know, for us to earn the, you know, earn the respect or the of the organization of the Raiders that have come before us, players and coaches. And that's something that we take really seriously. And uh we spent a lot of time this offseason talking about the history of the team and getting our players familiar with who are these faces around the building, who are, you know, who are the who are the great Raiders by position. And that's something really important to me that we educate the team, you know, on the on the history of this place. Coach, what what's the message sent to the players as they leave for summer break and before they return for training camp? >> Yeah. Uh well, you can ruin an offseason with 40 days away. You put all that work in this time of year. If you go post up on the couch, you know, all that work is for not. So 40 days away, you got to be really self-motivated. And we're not going to be with him every day, but uh you know, we'll be in contact with them. And then that's where uh that's where to me that, you know, Mr. Spitech, his job comes into play because he brought in a lot of quality individuals that are self motivated. If you don't have self motivated guys, um you have no idea what's coming once they come into training camp. So I feel really confident that we have self motiv motivated group. >> You got a sense how many players are staying here to work out? >> Yeah, we do. We have, you know, we have quite a few. Um and I think guys want to be here. We have we have the best of the best facilities, trainers, uh, weight staff, and our guys, you know, I know it's hard to hard to leave and find better than this place. So, uh, you know, Mr. Davis gives us the resources, and then our players, you know, want to stay, and that's a big advantage to our organization. >> He's he's feeling healthier than he has the last couple seasons and seems like rejuvenated out there. How much of that is a benefit or a luxury? Uh even when it comes to Fernando, like you don't have to rush him, especially if Kirk is firing on all cylinders. >> Yeah. You know, uh if you watch Kirk play, you know, his last four games in Atlanta, you know, you saw you saw what he can do. You know, he's getting healthier. He's played really good football for us uh this time of year and uh we're counting on him come the season. >> When Gruden was here, he did the early morning practice. His coach's players loved it because they're able to get out and go to their kids little league games, enjoy their families. Is that kind of what your thinking is? And do you anticipate continuing that through training camp, Clint? >> Well, I think uh you know, as far as the family part of it, our our family comes this next month. We get that time with our families and then you know, we're not going to see them a whole lot come training camp. The reason we're doing that is is you know, for our players to practice outside on the grass as much as possible. You know, there's such a benefit to them being on the grass and their bodies and their overall wellness. So, if we have to do that at 7:30 in the morning, that's what we got to do. Coach Kurt told us that he dispels the notion of him being a mentor in the quarterback's room despite, you know, his veteran status compared to the other two guys and he wants more of a collaborative effort. Is that something that knowing him from before you knew he'd kind of take that approach or did that surprise you? >> Um, you know, I never we never asked anybody to be a mentor. If you're on the roster, it's to play and to play really well for the team. So, um, that's the quarterback's job, all three of them, is to get ready to play and win games at a high level. And then uh you know when when everybody's doing that, they're pushing each other. It creates competition and the whole roster gets better. So all I want from our quarterbacks is to be competitive and to uh all prepare like their starters. >> As a first time head coach, you could talk to people and they can advise you on what it's all about and what to expect at least to this point. Has it been what you expected or have there been any like, oh wow, I got to take care of that as well and type of things. Yeah, I just think the our organization has surrounded myself with with so much talent with our with our scouts. Um, you know, can't say enough great things about Matt Capuro and Mike McCoy, uh, guys that I work with every day. Um, but, uh, you know, it's, you know, it's it's been a process that's been solely focused on making the making the football team better and have the best practice we can have. text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson and the Texans mini camp and their off seasonason have now concluded. It's time for summer break. title: The Dot: Breaking down the biggest takeaways from Saints OTAs
text: We are headed toward mini camp OTAs are over, so it is now full steam ahead to mini camp next week and then we'll hit the layover until training camp kicks off in July, but natural point to do a little bit of a look back at what we've seen and what we haven't seen and all the things that we want to see. So we're going to break that down on today's video, which is brought you by Matt Bowers Auto Group. My main thing so far throughout this camp is that I really do think that Taysom Hill looks like he's someone who has put in the work. Things are happening faster for him. The ball's coming out quickly. He's making smart aggressive throws. OTA 3 saw the defense play a little bit better than the offense who were clamping him down in seven-on-sevens, which I actually think is a good thing and something that we needed to see because I think the biggest questions with this team reside on that side of the ball, but in this setting Taysom Hill looks like confident. He looks like he's in command of the offense and he knows where he wants to go with the ball and he's trusting all of his receivers. And the best thing about it is is that Jordan Tyson and Chris Olave aren't doing anything. So he's out here making plays with a lot of guys that are going to be competing for spots four, five, and maybe six depending on how many people they carry at that position. So it isn't like he's just out here throwing the two top 11 picks against the defense that's still kind of trying to find its fit and its identity in the secondary. He's doing it with guys that might not be on the team and everybody looks good right now. So yes, it's a passing camp, but you can look back to how it was last year and at this time last year he looked like somebody that was trying to find his way. And right now he looks like a guy that knows the way, still needs to figure out how to get all the way there because it's only been one year and three days of OTAs, but definitely on the right path right now, definitely doing all the things that you want to see him do. And I think it's been a strong showing for him, and I think the arrow is still firmly up on him. So, nothing that's disappointed, and maybe even has solidified some of the optimism that everybody's kind of feeling right now. Long way to go, just getting started, but you can only start at one spot. So, for a June passing camp, seeing what you want to see. Second thing on my list plays in the number one. I I I think the receiver depth on this team is incredible. Jalen Polk has looked good. We saw Trey Palmer for the first time yesterday. He's looked good. Laviska Shenault has flashed in all the ways that you'd want to see him flashing. He looks good right now. Moves well, moving fast, looks healthy. All that's positive. Kevin Austin Jr. has probably the two best catches in this camp. He's somebody that looks like he deserves to be on an NFL team. That development process has just continued for him, and then Ronnie Bell kind of has come out of nowhere to be another guy that has flashed quite a bit. And then Barry and Brown made a nice play, and has looked good running routes. Um there's just a lot of guys right now that are making plays at wide receiver, and it's such a like a like a shocking difference overall when you really look at it, and you really think about it. Um you know, at times throughout history, I think the thing that that everybody remembers about this group uh is just we like the room, you know? And obviously, you're going back one, two, counting Rizzi, three staffs, three three head coaches to get to that that point in view, but it's just kind of existed for a while. It was Mike Thomas, and I think Emmanuel Sanders got here a little bit too late. Um you know, and and you know, it was it was it was Mike and Ted, but like it it's been a while since there's been real depth in that room. It's been Chris Olave and a bunch of guys, and like they've actually built it out right now, and to see everybody kind of shining and showing up where they want to show up. It's just it's a it's a different philosophy, you know? It's a it's a team that that values weapons, wants weapons, wants to stack weapons and I'm not sure that's always been the approach on on offense as weird as that sounds, it just feels like that's been a position where a lot of stuff has been taken for granted that the quarterback was going to elevate everybody and while I think this quarterback has the ability to be an elevator and already has shown that he is an elevator on third and long and some of these harder situations, it's a different build. Like there's guys here to help the quarterback, too, which, you know, that symbiotic relationship is just kind of kind of new here. So, seeing that I think it's been a really good thing and, you know, it's something that that I think it's just going to make it a better product to watch and I think that battle at wide receiver is going to be the best thing going on in camp and there's a lot of different ways that it could go right now. You could sprinkle a little a little bet on a bunch of people and I don't think any of them would be crazy. There's a lot of guys that I think could make a run and I I think this is a position where there's going to be somebody who gets cut that gets picked up by another team. There's just that much talent there right now and I think that there's a bunch of guys that that deserve to be on NFL rosters. So, that's a cool change and a cool thing to see and then my last thing is that I I I I just want to see the secondary continue to come into focus. Like I said, I thought day three of OTAs was the best day we've seen from them. They legitimately clamped down the first team offense. Um there were two plays where in seven-on-sevens where uh QB held the ball for a while and it was just beyond the point of like a reasonable, yeah, this is a real completion. Completion numbers still look good, but, you know, you're getting into four, five, six seconds in seven-on-sevens, you know, that that that just means there's good defense right now. So, strong showings from them. Um I think the arrow's up on Kool-Aid right now. He's had a couple pass breakups in this camp, has covered well. I've liked the way that that he's played. Uh you know, you see the signs from Riley, Sanker, you know, I think that's still coming together, but I think there's just a going to be an evidence gathering where it's just going to take a little while to know exactly what they have at all those positions and that's going to be the thing that defines the team on defense I I I think. Like we kind of know what the front is, we know what the the linebackers are going to be, we don't know what the secondary is going to be. And the secondary if they're if they're lights out it makes everything in front of them a little bit better and if they aren't it could make things a little bit harder, but I think there's the biggest swing of variance there where there's a lot of things that could be great and a lot of things that I don't know that the floor is set on them yet. You know, Kool-Aid's one where I think you know the floor is set and you're looking for the ceiling. Reed the floor set and you know, you Reed's defined. Like so, whatever on the other side of that Blackman could be a really good player if he stays healthy. So, there's a lot of stuff there that has to be defined. I really like the idea of Yonas Acker in the slot, but that's completely undefined. We've never seen him do it and I think Riley um played well last year, but cornerback's one of those positions where you can hit a small sample and you just got to keep getting reps until you really define it. So, there's just a lot of things that are seeking definition still. Not in a negative way, but just in a that way that that's legitimately unknown. So, I think that's something too where um you know, we're going to be looking at that all throughout camp. Two mini camp practices next week, so we'll get an eye on those. Um for everything else keep it locked in the world of South Florida football. We got your throw charge, your practice reports, your stories, extra podcasts, all kinds of stuff that you're not getting in these videos or in our podcast. So, sign up to the site. Uh we'll talk to you next time.
