Uh you know, obviously they feel they they have their time spent outside of the building uh to together more than others. Uh but, you know, just just seeing the impact, seeing the the the big guys up front and uh to seeing them really move the ball, uh it's really going to be something special down the line. when you've had two quarterbacks here in the huddle and working with two guys at different times, what has that process been like for you just as somebody that's trying to get on the same page and learning this offense as it exists with a different quarterback in the huddle at different times? >> Yeah. Uh I mean really don't I don't really care to me. Uh it's not really something that uh you know would help or you know not help me. Uh it it's really for them you know to to really get in getting uh situated with you know how we run our routes and uh the timing of things. is the concepts that we run. Uh but you know, for me, it's just running my route, catching the ball when it comes. Uh and it's not really too much of, you know, seeing the velocity of the ball or uh seeing the the how speed the speed of it. Uh it's just really just, you know, getting to that point that that spot, getting to that point, and and being ready to catch that ball. >> Justin, you went out to the to the girls tournament earlier this week and then obviously having the the winning team here today. just what do you appreciate about seeing kind of the the energy and the growth and and some of these women athletes connecting with the game that you love? >> Yeah. Yeah. I got a I got a chance to talk to a couple of them uh the other day and hey, chill out, man. My shot clock's still going. Um uh it was just really great to, you know, kind of talk to them and and kind of give them a little bit of motivational words uh before they started. Uh but it's just really crazy and and really inspiring to see the impact of the game and see the involvement of the game as much as it has come. I never would have expected to, you know, talk to some girl flag football team uh you know and and talking about really football and and really you know expanding the game uh to a whole different level. So, uh, it's really inspiring. I told them that they are really inspiring to the next generation, uh, of women that are coming up, girls that are coming up and wanting to play football and and make a difference and, uh, be a change, be something different, uh, in the world. So, uh, it's it's really impactful and, uh, I was really glad to be a part of it. >> Do you think as violent as this game is that you play now that someday a league might become a flag football team? >> Uh, that's a good question. It might be, you know, it might be later on down the line. But, uh, you know, right now it's just, uh, just trying to, you know, stay off the ground as much as possible. Uh, you know, not not really getting all of those hits, uh, that you don't want and, uh, just making sure that, you know, you're still in tune to everything. Uh, still getting that body right to make sure you're still feeling young out here. Justin, I know we've asked you this in previous years, but um as one of the team leaders, do you think you'll weigh in at all on the quarterback situation or do you anticipate that they'll ask you what I mean coaches or whoever ask you and how will you handle that knowing that you're probably friends with both of them and like and the whole thing? >> Yeah. Um I feel like at the end of the day it's it's more going to be a coaches um a coach's call just from you know what they see in training camp uh the different plays that they are making the adjustments being a leader being a vocal leader all of those different things that goes into what we're looking for and uh at the end of the day somebody's going to have that job. Uh whether it's Kyler whether it's JJ. Uh so it's just all about working with both of them to to make sure that uh whoever is the starter uh you know we're dialed in. are ready to go and uh the connection, the the relationship, all of that is dialed in and and and you know, ready to go uh when the season starts. >> What you've seen from JJ this spring compared to last year, where have you seen him change or where have you seen him develop? >> Yeah, I've seen him change a lot. Uh which is normal, you know, being a a young quarterback in this league and having a year under his belt, you know, you get to learn a couple things. you get to learn uh how to be, you know, a professional, how to uh really, you know, take care of your body, take care of uh your arm, you know, and obviously take care of your mind. Uh so I feel like he's definitely uh gotten a little bit more smarter uh into reading the different coverages, uh under understanding the different throws uh that he's making. Everything doesn't have to be 100 miles per hour. Uh you know, just some throws, you know, can put a little touch on it and get it to the spot. Uh so I feel like that is uh you know one of his most impactful uh improvements that he has made. Uh and and it's just about continue to work with him. Uh continue to understand uh you know JJ and understand uh K1 as well. Uh they're are two different guys and they are two different quarterbacks. Uh they both throw differently. They both have a different mindset. Uh so it's just all about you know just continue to be uh work with them continue to you know have um have the work outside of this building and uh during the season uh during the summertime uh get with them and make sure we're dialed in them. >> Justin, how important to the leadership group was it to have Aaron Jones come back? >> Very important. Very important. I mean he's a he's a great guy. That's my that's my dog. That's my that's my buddy. Yeah. And and he really understands how to be a leader. he understands um you know how to be a a a good person. Uh that's the main impactful thing. Not just him on the football field, but uh him coming in this locker room having a smile smile on his face no matter what's going on. Uh he's always talking to you. He's always asking you what's going on uh in your mind and and making sure you're good. So, uh having him back on his team is definitely impactful uh you know on and off the field. and adding of course adding to that room uh that is already impactful with with JP and the rest of the guys uh in that running back room. >> Last one. >> Oh yeah, last one or >> last one. Okay, sorry. I'm wonder uh at receiver. So beyond yourself, Addison, and Jennings, who has caught your eye uh for playing well? >> That's a tough one. Uh everybody. Uh that's a that's a hard one. Tai has definitely been uh coming on the scene. Uh J2 uh has been coming on the scene. Um, I mean, all all of the guys have been really improving uh at a tremendous rate. Uh, every single time that they come out here, um, you know, I'm definitely coaching them and making sure that, you know, everybody is is held responsible and and have those high expectations for everybody to come out here and, you know, be a a Justin Jefferson, be a Jordan Addison. Uh, so it it's really holding those standards high to everybody and, uh, everybody can have a chance to be on that field. you know, it's not really a main obviously, you know, the three guys that are at the top of the list, but uh beyond that, anybody can step up and be a playmaker on special teams, on offense. Uh so, it's just coming to work, just like I tell tell the guys, coming to work, uh making sure that you know, you're getting better every single time you're coming out here. Uh so, I definitely been seeing improvements from every single person that's uh out there on that field at receiver. Thank y'all. Appreciate it.

title: Kevin O'Connell Talks Caleb Banks, Player Development & Vikings Offensive Line | Minnesota Vikings
text: All right, let's get uh let's get started. I want to uh first off today um you know take a moment uh we had some very special visitors uh to our final mini camp practice uh today from uh you know recognizing the state champions. Come on in. Come on in, guys. From Rosemount High School, the Irish. Uh we've got Coach Erdman here. Congratulations, coach. And then we've got Olivia. >> Yes, >> Olivia is a safety. And then uh Taylor, I got those names right, is a wide receiver. So you guys go up against each other in practice. >> Yeah, I guess. >> Does it does it ever get heated? >> A little bit. >> Okay, good. But I got a chance to uh go out to uh the the games that were going on here at our facility. Uh nothing is better than when, you know, we're bringing in people uh to take part in in in events here at our facility and going down there. The energy, the enthusiasm. Got a chance to talk to you guys before your games. I don't know if uh my speech did any good, but uh it was fun to hear about how the championship game went. And uh obviously for me, you know, I think I mentioned it to you guys. I have two daughters and the fact that you guys are paving the way and making flag football uh what it is and and where we all hope that it goes from here. But I got to say, watching the football, it was I mean, you guys are really really talented. It was competitive. Um it was phenomenal to be a part of that. I know Justin Jefferson was out there. Um, our new GM, Nolan Teasley, was out there, and we were all kind of taken back by just the energy, the passion, the enthusiasm, and, uh, just your, uh, ability to help continue to promote the game. Years and years from now, people will remember teams like yours, uh, as the early state champions of, of many for years to come. And you guys helped pave the way for that to happen. So, welcome. We're glad you guys were here with us and really appreciate it. Congrats once again. >> Thank you. >> Yeah, you got it. You got it. So, the other thing I want to mention today, you guys probably saw some other coaches, uh, you know, out here. We do have our Bill Walsh Fellowship coaches, uh, here. They'll also be back in training camp. So, I want to make sure you guys have their names. We've got Isaiah Bishop, PJ Burkhalter, uh, Deshawn Haney, Jonathan Lloyd, and then two former players, uh, which I'm sure you guys recognize, Tristan Jackson, and Bobby McCain, both taking part, uh, which you guys know we have Ben Ben Ellison on the staff full-time now. uh part of a passion of of mine and uh the wolves is to continue to you know welcome our own you know back in for other roles and responsibilities as they transition um out of football. So they they'll be around and and hopefully you guys get to get a chance you know to meet what we consider a strong group of developing coaches you know for the future uh here in the NFL wrapping up the offseason program today. I just told the team uh for a voluntary uh camp, I know mini camp is mandatory, but uh when you have the same group here for the better part of all of your OTAAS and phase one and phase 2, um with all the things these guys have going on, um it is really really cool to have the the participation level, uh the buy in, the the hunger to continue to raise the foundation of of where we've what what's been built by our players here, but ultimately where we want to go um as a as a team. So, compliments to those guys. I think they're ready uh for training camp. I think they're ready uh to pick up right where we left off as we kind of fully enter the competition phase of being able to build our team and kind of chase what our ceiling is going to be for the season. Um as far as the quarterbacks, I thought those guys, you know, once again, uh both of them and really, uh you know, all four of those guys, but really JJ and and Kyler both had really good days. Again, still plenty of opportunities to learn. Um Flo's guys are giving us great looks. Our defense is playing fast, humming around uh mid-season form in a lot of ways, which shows just uh what those guys are able to do over there, even with a lot of young players on that side of the ball. But excited about both where where both those guys are at. Um looking forward to them, you know, using the time from now until we report back to continue to kind of build on uh on what they've really accomplished, which is a lot. Um both those guys, you know, have done some really, really good things and I think they're elevating our football team because of it. So excited to get back when we get a chance to get going uh in training camp, but I'll open it up to you guys. >> Many worry that Kyler brought it up yesterday that whoever ends up as QB1 will be missing out on some reps or is that just a necessary evil in the competition? >> Yeah, you know, I I uh you know, I don't necessarily know if you know, it was it was more about you know, hearing you know, kind of the full quote. You know, I know what he was intending. It was very similar to conversations we've had um privately and even as a group, you know, with me in the quarterback room a little bit more. I would say this, you know, this phase this time of year, you know, based by the rules and also how we handle it. Um it is a foundation uh to build off of and every rep obviously matters, but this time of year, the beauty of not going full speed on a lot of reps is you can get a lot out of watching other guys reps as well. So, um I think that's taken place. I think there's been great learning uh that's taken place, but those guys both know um we, you know, we have a a plan in place to to make sure that the decision we make that is going to be about what's best for the Minnesota Vikings. And the timeline of that does involve making sure we get our starter uh ready to go. And u you know, we want to make sure by the time we play the Green Bay Packers that there's been ample time to, you know, have you know, the best possible offense we can have uh to help our football team and the quarterback's going to play a big role in that. Um, so that was uh, you know, that's kind of where where we're at right now as far as like the timeline goes. Uh, you know, I think to give a an actual date would be um, not necessarily accurate from a portrayal of how we see it, but there is a timeline to make sure that we can allow the competition to to continue and advance and and really lay out a training camp that will allow us to do that. uh but also make uh a timely decision knowing that through all of this um not just those two but Carson's had a really good spring and Max has come along and those guys are getting really minimal reps. So even though um those those guys are splitting those reps, they're splitting a lot of reps because, you know, Carson obviously where he's at in his career is capable of, you know, applying a lot of things to our offense without a ton of reps and and Max is getting a lot of the development work that quite honestly as an undrafted guy last year who we absolutely love. Um you know, wish we could have, you know, had a little bit maybe slower timeline than needing to play all three of those guys last year. future lights that you'll when training camp starts the early part of camp it'll be similar to what we're seeing out here just from our point of view in terms of reps and >> just with the just with the different volumes of days like some days you're you know will be those classic two hour two and a half hour there'll be massive amounts of work um where maybe it could be split but I I wouldn't read much into who gets what on which days I know me saying that was the waste of the time that I took to say it uh but I will say uh that uh we're going to put together a way where we can you know the different aspects of situational football that they need to get uh the call periods will obviously be massive um periods where they don't necessarily know what's coming because that's what football is and that's the challenge for you know Kyler to get to a place where that comfort level is there and and more so you know even to the other question just what I think Kyler was speaking about was just being a little uncomfortable um which I I don't want to speak for you guys but a lot of the real growth we've all probably had in life comes in those uncomfortable times where you work through it and and you find a way out the other side and you're that much better off for it. And that's I know that's Kyler's uh mentality towards it. And you know, much like JJ's early time here, he's using his experience uh in the system in a really good way. But at the same time, he's still applying some really detailed things that um I think he's done a really good job of from the time the season ended till now. So, it is very competitive. Um it is, like I said, making our team better. I think our players are are seeing that every single day uh with how the even these days went and I'm sure they'll feel that early on, but ultimately what's best for the Minnesota Vikings is going to be the direction we go uh to win football games and and move the ball and score points. >> Where have you seen with counter the most growth, whether it's like verbiage or reprogression like some of those specifics? What has stood out the most? >> Yeah, I think all of it. you know, the the one thing about the these times and really training camp in many ways can be can be difficult as well because you're systematically installing things, but just because you installed something in the first day doesn't mean you don't run it again. So, you're really layering uh the learning for these guys and uh you try to put it together in a way where everything kind of fits like a puzzle piece. But sometimes, especially against the defense we play against every day, uh there is an element of, you know, we've got to really expand uh to not let them limit our volume of kind of how we're playing. So, I think he's handled that well. But there's always a point where, you know, you can feel that overflow uh start to happen and then you acknowledge where that point is and then you figure out a way uh really in many ways it's going to be Kyler over the summer really diving back into things and making sure by the time we come back and he's learning. The beauty of it is it's not going to be the first time he's learning uh the majority of the things that we're doing. Um but, you know, he's made a ton of really really impressive throws. He's layered the football. He's drove it down the field. He's checked the ball down, you know, to avoid sacks and things that are really positive for the position. And we really haven't even been able to see his true athleticism impact the position either. Um, so I'd say he's improved massively calling plays and just running the show and it will only continue to get better. Um, as both those guys continue to push to help make our team better. >> Talk about having a date in mind. Is that for to pick a starter in your mind or just to separate one guy to go to more first team reps like that? >> I think that's that's a great question because I think it could be, you know, I think it as transparent as I can possibly be, I think that question or which question you're answering answers itself. Sometimes it might be this is the guy and we're going full send. Sometimes it might be there's been some separation and we want to maybe use another phase or a joint practice or two or even a preseason game or two to try to, you know, help finish that so that the question ultimately is who is the starter. Um, but like I said, you know, part of this with the, you know, the limited time you do have is, you know, you've got to put it put it together in a way that challenges those guys and see who responds, see who handles adversity well, uh, and ultimately see who elevates the offense and and regardless of what we've been this year's version of the offense because it's going to look different at times. We're going to do some different things and that player that elevates the group as a whole is going to be the guy uh, that's under center against the Green Bay Packers. Kevin, do you foresee um both of them playing in the preseason then Kevin or are you probably going to have a decision by that time? >> Um once again kind of goes hand in I I see both of them playing um in regards to you know who plays first and all those things or what we've you know communicated. I will say this like the communication is going to be paramount from me to you guys and and ultimately our fan base. You guys are the extension that helps us communicate with our fans. like there's not going to be any, you know, there's no I don't really see any competitive reasons. This isn't a game week where we we may be trying to uh, you know, not disclose things. I think this is going to be training camp's open. You know, it's an open competition. Um, and I want to see these guys in a very very uh unique and in many ways difficult circumstance elevate themselves and their games to to help the Minnesota Vikings. >> Wes talked a little bit yesterday about it's kind of an upward arrow for JJ. Where have you seen that show up or what's been your assessment of him throughout the off? >> I mean, I think it's been physical uh with his fundamentals and and the way he's really tried to apply uh you know, the different types of throws. He now has the experience and and you're not talking about hypotheticals anymore. You know, he can learn plays based upon reps. In many ways, he's seeing himself up on the board when either myself or Wes are installing those plays. and then he knows he's worked on a lot of those throws and the rhythm and the timing and the trajectory of those throws. Um, then he gets to come out and practice them and then he gets to go into at least the seven on sevens and compete and try to apply those things. And uh, you guys have probably seen it. I know you're not out here every day, but you guys have seen him, you know, make some of those throws. And it's just been fun to watch him just totally dive in uh, to an individual improvement plan for the betterment of of the group. And vice versa with Kyler coming into a brand new offense uh totally different than what he's been a part of and him be comfortable uh being uncomfortable uh and pushing through and and and continuing to grow in in his own lane of of what this is because they're not two players that have both been in our system for three years. They're at different points, different points of their career. All that applies, but at the same time, it's ultimately very simple answer in the end. what's best for the Minnesota Vikings to win games and activate, you know, the the really good players we have around them in that offensive huddle. >> Talk about somebody separating from the other. Like, are there data points you're looking for that will tell you that or is it more of a feel thing that >> Yeah, I mean, we're, you know, we track everything, so there's obviously data involved, but I, you know, I think there's a le a layer of feel to it from them and us. you know, some things where, you know, maybe we didn't spend 20 minutes in the meeting that morning, but we've talked about that and they apply it in a in a period where uh it's real football. There's no scripts. There's no, you know, we're calling plays. Flo's calling it. He's the best in the league at what he does. He makes it really hard for all of us every single day. And at the same time, we need to make sure we're not just only preparing for the Minnesota Vikings cuz we will not play our defense. There's a reason why Flo's here, so we don't have to play against them. Um, and and that makes training camp difficult. There's high stress that goes into that with 11 players up at the line of scrimmage on some snaps. And uh I I love every aspect of it because I think uh these guys are handling it in such a great way that uh they're both going to massively improve and you know it's it's probably going to end up being a difficult decision just based on where I know those guys are going to go. Kevin for >> Yeah, I think you guys probably s saw him working uh you know on the side field yesterday. Uh we've gotten, you know, we've received really really positive uh reviews. Um had the offseason continued, he probably would have um you know, started to get some work in some of the individual drills and then progress him into some of the the team stuff. But I will say this, you know, the feedback I'm getting from the coaches, uh, Ryan Nielsen, Flo, Pad Hill, um, has been, you know, phenomenal as far as his ability to hear information, retain it, and apply it. Just there's a lot of different ways we can be activating Caleb's brain and the above the neck challenge of learning Flo's intricate system. I got it. I know Justin, you got places to be. U, but, uh, but I'm excited. Uh, I'm excited about where he's at. And that's not even talking about, you know, the big reason to be excited about Caleb is the physical ability and presence of a guy that big, that strong, that fast, you know, in the middle of your defense. >> I do. >> Yeah, I do. Go ahead. You >> talked about the O line and a lot this spring. Just how satisfied were you or have you been with that work? >> It's been phenomenal. I mean, and you know, hopefully you guys in in the limited time you've been out have maybe even noticed it. Keith's done a phenomenal job with that group. um both in the meeting room and on the field. It feels uh every single day feels like there's such a purpose to what they're trying to do. Play style has been a term that that we've used um many many times, you know, over the years and and that is the mentality of what we want to build. Those guys have very very high expectations of themselves and Keith is driving that. We got great leaders in the room with Bo CD. I mean, guys, uh, you know, have done it here for a long time. And then Frank Smith's ability to come in and really apply some layers to our offense uh that uh have really helped me uh helped Wes, helped our staff, and and I think our players are excited about the direction that we go. All that means nothing till we put the pads on, but they've done everything uh to have me really excited about their potential when football comes around. >> Thanks, everybody. Thanks guys.

title: Setting Expectations For Kyler Murray
text: Kyler Murray has a great chance to earn his place in the driver's seat of the Minnesota Vikings, but what does he have to do to keep that going? >> You are Locked On Vikings, [music] your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Podcast Network. Your team every day. >> What's going on everybody? Welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast where we're all just trying to learn something new. It's part of the Locked On Podcast Network, the number one sports podcasting network. Today on the show, I would like to expand the conversation about Kyler Murray beyond the immediate ramifications of where he is at with the team. Uh you know, this like QB competition or not a competition whatever you want to call it. Uh at some point, Kyler Murray will take snaps for the Vikings. I think it would be pretty a pretty crazy outcome if he didn't, right? I don't think anybody expects that. And that means that he's going to get an opportunity to take the job, keep the job, and maybe even get an extension in the job. And so today, I want to go over what exactly it's going to take for him to be declared the starting quarterback, if that's something the Vikings are even going to do. For him to entrench himself as the starter even if he gets hurt. And also for him to earn an extension, which is very much on the table and something that it's even been reported kind of softly that the Vikings are maybe clearing a little bit of money out for next year. And part of the reason they did did this off season is so that they can afford to give Kyler Murray a big old QB contract if he earns one. Well, what does earning one look like? What does earning the starting job look like? What do we need to see from Kyler Murray to give him all the reps with the ones that we haven't seen so far because we haven't seen anything cuz it's just the start of OTAs. Um so we'll start with the short term, right? What is it going to take for the Vikings to stop beating around the bush and give Kyler Murray the job as it sounds like by all the reports he is in the driver's seat for, right? He's still splitting reps with J.J. McCarthy. Um I saw somebody point out and I had noticed as well McCarthy's still taking snaps in those like warm-ups. This is sounds weird, but this is actually a really big indicator of like where these guys are actually at. Who are they taking the snaps from? Like which center when they warm up just like the under center snaps and like play action footwork and stuff. Who are they taking the snaps from? McCarthy is taking snaps from Blake Brandel. Kyler Murray is taking snaps from Michael Jergens. Um so, you could either say Michael Jergens surprise he's center one right now and nobody expected that or you could say J.J. McCarthy right now is sitting at the de facto the kind of meaningless distinction of QB1, which is I think where he has sat and he has since the start of OTAs. People got very mad at me for pointing that out, but it has remained true. but that's a meaningless distinction, right? Because we're not actually finalizing any depth chart stuff or anything like that. It's just somebody's got to take snaps from this guy, somebody's got to take snaps from that guy, but in terms of like what you put who you put in which cell right now that might be important. And that there also is a and a downstream effect of that. Not unlike what we talked about yesterday with Kyler Murray and the point that he made that he's getting heat for for some reason, but it's a really good point. Hey, you know, if he's in this QB competition that's actually kind of reducing the efficacy of OTAs for him. It's it's it's not that useful to have to split reps in a competition when you're trying to learn the offense and you're trying to get there and you you know, it's not that useful to have to give up half of your first team reps to the other guy. Um and that really really doesn't make sense if the battle is a foregone conclusion, right? If they're still trying to figure out who they want to say and they were they're looking for certain things and they're trying to see a certain criteria from Kyler Murray before they give him the keys to the castle, then it makes sense to kind of make him go through this rigmarole. And and and that is what I'm like interpreting this whole thing as, right? Hey, go earn it. And here's what you need to do to earn it and we have confidence that you'll be able to do it, but you don't get to win a game just by showing up to it, right? I've been comparing this a little bit to like Ohio State versus Akron, right? That game starts 0-0 and Ohio State's going to win it just about every time, they still have to show up and do it. You have to go through that process, right? You can maybe take it as a given and look away and be really surprised if if you look up and Akron has won and maybe you don't even want to watch that game, but it's going to have to happen. You still got to show up and do it and and kind of prove yourself, right? And until you do that, you're taking snaps from Michael Jordan's and you're not going to get to build that chemistry with Blake Brandel, which that that is again I I cost I think is real in this kind of spring OTA program, which is where you line up stuff like Blake Brandel getting used to snapping to a shorter quarterback, which feels important because he did send one over Carson Wentz's head last year and Carson Wentz is a very tall quarterback. Uh and so I I would like to get that chemistry down. You can also do that in camp if you want to declare a starter. But that's the other thing, will Kevin O'Connell even declare a starter? He didn't do it last year. There was never any point where he said J.J. McCarthy is our starter. Um the media made kind of a thing out of it. I don't think anybody expected Sam Howell to be the starter and when all was said and done, he wasn't even on the team and he was replaced by Carson Wentz. Um but O'Connell never actually made the formal declaration that J.J. McCarthy is our guy, he's going to start, he's going to be our dude. And I wonder if he doesn't again. This is a different circumstance where they have billed this as a competition. They said there is a QB battle going on, and they didn't have that last year. They didn't sell it last year as J.J. McCarthy is battling with Sam Howell. McCarthy took the first-team reps. Howell took the second-team reps, and and it never changed. So, we could see O'Connell respond to this differently because it is a different circumstance, but I'm not 100% sure about that because O'Connell hasn't declared starters in other position battles, either. When you've had, you know, a corner going toe-to-toe or something like that, right? Or or who's going to win at guard between Blake Brandel and Donovan Jackson? They never said, "Hey, we're going to start Donovan Jackson. Great Great news. The battle's decided. We made our choice. Donovan Jackson is our starter." He's not going up on the podium and saying that. So, you might not even get that formal declaration. title: Jeremy Springer: "Competition's Great." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Ken? >> Can you bring in a lot of new players who have special teams experience? Is it like a puzzle for you trying to fit them in the into the right slots or seeing how many different spots that they can play and how you utilize them? >> Yeah, it's a great question. I I I just think as you go through OTAs, you try to figure out what kind of guy this is, how smart he is, what kind of football intelligence he has throughout the years, where he's played at, and then you kind of look at the roster overall and and you start figuring out who's going to make the team, who might not make the team, and you kind of just start plugging and placing, and I think training camp at the beginning that that first couple weeks into the first joint practice is really big cuz you just really see guys that truly excel and their learning and it's compounding and they get better and it's like, all right, well this guy's probably going to fit here. This guy's probably going to fit here, and it just kind of over the years with experience you just kind of figure it out. Uh but it play it usually plays itself out the way it should. If I if that makes any sense, I think it does. >> Like I read about, you know, a couple rookies who have special teams experience, and how different is it for them from from what they do in college to here? >> Yes, very different now. Especially with kickoff kickoff return. It's such a different game. Like the rules are different, the way we punt's different, the formations, when you can release. I think there's such a um there's such a huge learning curve going from college to NFL now. So, you just got to look at the movements, like how they move well, how they talk, how confident they are. It's like their overall athletic ability. You just know at some point it's going to click. Elijah Ponder's a perfect example. Like he came in last year and was a good player at his Division 1 double A school in California, didn't know anything about special teams, but you can see the athletic part about him. And if eventually it clicked for him, and he got better and better until he was, you know, full-time guy for us, four-core guy. I just think you have to look at the movement skills and see how smart and how they how they how they learn and compound things, and I think it's going to at some point click for those guys, and hopefully it translates to them helping us on on teams. >> Thank you. >> Yeah, no problem. >> With the with the with the good skill stuff? >> Yeah. >> How was how was um you jamming? Has he been >> Has he been using him in that regard? >> Of course. He's running back, man. I mean, running backs, dude, they're going to they're going to be highly involved. And he played special teams in Alabama. And he was a pretty good player there on special teams. So, he already has a foundation of playing special teams and knowing what it is to to run out on punt, which most guys don't do on offense. So, he has that background experience to where I think it helps him a little bit right now. >> How's been the last few days with the Andre? >> How's been fine. It's been good. Yeah, it's always good to have some competition in or or guys that want to try that are going to try out for us. So, it's always good to keep us updated. But, I think bringing competition is always good for everybody. >> Would you have Would you consider obviously you guys did it at kicker last summer, right? Did you in training camp? Would you consider doing that again for the the punter side? >> At the end of the day, like I don't I it's not my job to make the roster moves, you know, that's up to Elliot, coach Rayborn, and Ryan, all those guys. I just think, you know, competition's great. If we can do it, I I love a a position I I love one at each position. We could. We just don't have the number for that. And whatever what the team needs is what the team needs. So, if we bring him in, great. If we don't, then whatever we have on the team, we got to live with. Thank you. >> How would Bryce be if that was the case? If you had two Is he the kind of guy who >> He's a competitor, man. I mean, he started a small school in Illinois, and he worked his way to Michigan State. So, I think he's got that mentality in him to be like, "Hey, whoever they bring in, I want to beat them out, and I'm going to be the starter." So, I would hope to see that at any position that we have on this team. >> Uh last thing for you. What's the focus today? Is it Is there something specific that you wanted to work on before guys go away for the >> I want I want us to have a good punt day, a good field goal day, and leave on a good note and the training camp when it gets real. >> All right, man. >> All right, brother. Appreciate you, dog. Appreciate you as always. >> Thanks. >> No, no, you're good. >> You're good.

title: Zak Kuhr: "It's a Good Group." | Patriots Press Conference
text: All right. What's going on? >> Uh talked to Christian far more later on today. Just kind of you see from him last year maybe his growth continues. How good can he be as >> Yeah, I think with Christian he's done a great job uh from last year to this spring. Uh I mean, they're working their asses off and it is it's a good group. It's a good group of people. uh you know, as we do like our team families every Wednesday, you get to learn more about these guys and they're just a great group of people that are taking full advantage of every opportunity they get. >> Tech, who did you uh reach out to or maybe lean on this offseason as you're preparing, you know, for full time in the defensive coordinator role? >> Um I wouldn't say that. I mean, it's been pretty the same as last year. So >> I guess with the whole offse, >> yeah, I mean I would say even the same things that uh T did last year were very similar too because we have very much the same philosophy of how we believe things should be done. Uh and it's not the one difference I would say from last offseason to this offseason as a staff is it's not year one conversations now. It's more how can we develop it and grow it more than what is than just hey day one like how are we teaching cover two you know there's some more uh in-depth advanced conversations >> facility particularly off the field >> uh I don't know if that really has much to do with it I very much appreciate the new facility but it's more about the people inside the building than the actual things inside the building >> the technology offices uh I don't know. I'd have to sit down and think about that for I'm still finding new rooms in the building myself. So, >> Shane, >> yeah, I was excited. You know, Shane's a good friend of mine. Uh like I said the other day, he's been very uh influential in me and my development as a coach, and it it probably I probably wouldn't be standing here without him. So, uh, I was grateful for the opportunity. He brought me with him to New York and he's just another great sounding board when I have questions and, you know, you, you know, he's going to give me the true honest answer. There's a deep enough of relationship there for it. >> You expect might be some changes leaguewide. You know, this a time to kind of study other teams, seem to up on the schedule, but Jan was talking the other day about kind of getting ahead of problems before they present themselves. >> Yeah. And I think that's the beauty of being in a year or two of the same system is now you can kind of find those problem plays rather than just really honing in on your own stuff uh around the league and you can kind of like Jam said, you can kind of beat it to the punch. And those are the the things you can work in the spring of things we might see and we know there are concept testers. Uh things that might really test your rules and some tough plays and teaching the guys these are the weaknesses within the scheme and this is what we really need to pay attention to. And along with that uh having this continuity for the second straight year is now we can go try to try some new things. go in the lab, try some new things, some new coverages, some new pressures, uh, and put it to work. Right now, >> some of those new things in the red zone, we've seen you there virtually all camp. >> I would say, uh, there's not one specific place where we're not trying new things. So, red zone, first, second down, third down, situational stuff. I think you can always take advantage of time where you can start trying some things uh that you put some some good effort into studying the offseason but it's not just in one particular area. >> Coach Booker just mentioned making some enhancements. I think you didn't want to give away too much in the red zones specifically now you guys have been out here a little bit. Have you seen that kind of pay dividends and what >> Yeah. And to Andrew like what he just said like we're trying some new things. Uh we're trying to do some enhancements some even just some communication and and feeling and you know during the season I believe we had the fewest amount of trips to the red zone uh which is a good thing. Now we were not anywhere near where we wanted to be as far as production down in there. But you know is that a lack of reps and whatnot as far as within the game? You know I don't know that. But it's good to now the guys are hearing the concepts and the words for the second straight year and they kind of understand a little bit better and then the communication be a little bit better. >> I just want to ask you when it comes to tempo from the defenses quickly. Do you find that advantageous to you guys or >> you're saying like from a schematic purpose? I mean, I would say the work of doing it is great for us, how we're doing it right now because it always keeps you on your feet, uh, on your toes, you know, having done both offense and defense and having coached an uptempo no huddle offense before, there there are pros and cons to it. And as long as you are decisive and on the same page, right? And kind of that's what the offense is trying to do. They're trying to kind of catch you in a law or or catch you off guard, but if you can still work your disguise because you know what the call is going to be or the call comes in early and now they can't do as much pre- snap until they, you know, start going on the ball then hard counting all that stuff. But if they're going on the ball, snapping right away, you can you can dictate a little bit defensively. Yeah, I don't want you staying up at night worrying about the run defense, [laughter] >> you know. I think Yeah, I mean the players have a big part of that, but I believe they're getting better at working the technique. You know, sometimes it's a mix of things. You know, whether it be, hey, you're going into a game plan thinking this and you didn't get that and, you know, it hurts you early. Uh, potential movements that, you know, based off the study of the film, it was great for it, but now the game plan changed. So, they caught us early that we adjust all that. Yeah. I mean, injuries always play a factor into it, obviously, but again, this is kind of the first year of these guys hearing how we teach the run game technique. And it goes, you know, both ways. A two-way street. Teams learn you from as much more film uh is put on tape, just like we learn them. So, you know, hopefully, well, not hopefully, I can assure the guys on our team that we're going to work it every day and we all understand that we have to earn the right to rush. And I think those guys understand that. I think they're going to take great pride in how we play the run early and often. You >> earn the right to rush on the first couple. >> That's right. That's right. Or even get into second and 10 and make it more of a passing down. But they got to understand that earning the right to rush, earning the right to go earn money, you know, for their own uh contracts is uh a big part of being stout in the run. >> How much familiarity with each other? >> Yeah, that's that's a huge part. Yeah, like we said early on the year, I mean, you know, we had some good games early in the year, but we had a lot of new guys working with, you know, new guys, and this spring has been huge, man, of guys just learning each other. And you should see some of the conversations that Kevin Bard and Spain are having on the sideline just so they can feel each other out and know where each other going to be cuz chemistry and coordination is shoot a a huge part of it. Huge part of it. And the more we can be with disguise with execution and the more they can be coordinated and have that chemistry. >> Yeah. Yeah, I mean the sky's limit in run game, pass game, res, anything. >> I'm wonder what the offensive trends in the game. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Yeah. More tight end packages. You're seeing a lot more often. You know, we usually do a study of how much base defense we really play over the past years, five, six years, and it's typically going down, down, and down because it's a passing length passing league. And then over the past uh over last year, you can see the base packages coming up. And you know, offensive corners are doing a good job of using formation indicator uh indicator to indicate man and zone and displace bigger skill bodies that typically aren't out at number one at receiver or number two, number three, whatever it mean. And try to get you into bigger packages so they can try to, you know, kind of like what uh uh you know, McVey and the Rams were doing, trying to get bigger packages, uh get the defense bigger packages so they can maybe spread it out more to throw it. And you just got to kind of play the game with them. And you know, I would say one of my biggest philosophies is you want to be sound and know what you're doing as a defense. Okay, everybody be on the same page. But the more multiple we can get within different packages and hey, maybe this time we're showing you this personnel package and not this or maybe this time it's this. Appreciate you guys. Yes.

What does it mean to get away last year from spending a year working with Christian Barour as a player and a person and how do you feel about him moving forward? >> Well, a very disruptive player, you know, a player that cares a lot and he's a player that, you know, we have to we have to manage and so, you know, he's able to get and understand what to do without, you know, practicing every single day. and uh you know just uh want to see him finish we you know he so does he but some of those plays that he had in the back field around a quarterback and instead of being disruptive being able to to finish those and because he did that a lot and uh try not to you know try to talk to him about not being frustrated you know that those plays impact the game and it may not show up on a statistical you know category and you know but I think his attitude has been great. I think uh enjoy working with him. I I do and uh looking for for more and more of the same next year. >> What does it mean for a quarterback to be a step ahead of the defense and what are some of the tools or uh anticipatory elements that can allow them to have that advantage? >> Well, you always want to have the pen last and you know, well, they run this, we're going to do this. But, I mean, as you saw last season when he did play for the Eagles in the few games that he did, he still has some juice left. >> Yeah, I was surprised because I'm thinking, hey, if he wants to play again, 33 years old, could he be that rotational piece that fits in nicely here or did something kind of go awry here that forced him to retire, then get released, and maybe sign elsewhere? Cuz wouldn't he be a guy that you would have interest in? >> Well, they always say never say never, but the abruptness of the way that that happened, it was a little odd and it could have been for a multitude of reasons, but he's not going to command the amount of Remember, this is a defense and Vic Fangio who typically deploys or utilizes only three edge rushers in his rotation. So, if you're Zidarius Smith and you want to play at 33 years old, you're likely going to want to undertake a more prominent role and I just that's not going to happen in Philadelphia. They're already three deep and you have Arnold Ebiketie who they signed to a two-year deal. They just signed A.J. Up Enesa, so to me it just never felt like like Philadelphia would be would be the next place that he resumes his career. >> Uh we'll get you out with this. Andrew DiCecco Football 4. Make sure you check out the Inside the Birds podcast and all Andrew's stuff over at Uh just a couple guys that you that stood out to you in these OTAs that now you might pay closer attention to at training camp. >> Yeah, great question. So, I I would say linebacker Chance Campbell. That's a player that the Eagles seem to like a little bit. He was on the practice squad all of last season. Signed just a few days before the preseason finale, but he does have overlap in Tennessee with linebackers coach Bobby King. So, the the team is was clearly familiar with what he can bring. He did have an ACL injury August of 2024, so maybe that had to do with his late arrival, but his pathway to the roster would be on special teams and he would have to compel the Eagles to keep five linebackers, but I I keep an eye on how players are deployed and and what their alignment is and at least in the spring they they've given him he was working with the first unit in the the the punt the punt group. And I think even in an earlier spring session with the first group on kickoff. So, we'll we'll see what happens, but I thought he also did some nice things as a linebacker playing with the second team opposite Smile Mondon Jr. And I guess another player, if you want somebody that's a little bit off the beaten path, it would be an offensive tackle by the name of Jarrid Dillard who was signed as an undrafted free agent in 2023 by the Tennessee Titans out of Boise State. Played in I believe 16 games, started some of those games, started maybe nine of those games. But, we go back to the inexperience of the offensive line aside from Fred Johnson. And maybe he's a player that if you feel comfortable with him when you cross train him, if you cross train him, that he gives you a little bit more seasoning when it comes to adding an experienced player there. He's gotten a lot of second team work at at tackle at both tackle spots. And he's also I think even wrapped it right guard as well. So, obviously it's in the early stages, but it is something that I'm filing away for training camp. >> Love it. Training camp last year was July 22nd, so I would imagine sometime in that range the birds will be back. We'll do our division previews. We'll look all around the NFL. We got a lot going on this summer for Football 4 Andrew DiCecco and the boys over at Inside the Birds got you covered. And of course we do here on Football 4 Andrew. Always a pleasure, man. >> Likewise, Mike. Take care. >> I enjoy talking to Andrew each and every week here on Football 4 on The Sports Bash live on 97.3 ESPN.

title: Grey Zabel: "The Offense Feels Extremely Close To Being The Same" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Appreciate the announcement by the way. How we doing? Good. How you doing? Good. >> How's all has life changed as a Super Bowl champion? Does it mean it anything? >> Not really. Um just a few more people notice you in public, but other than that, it's just getting back to work and preparing for this upcoming season. >> How about year two? We hear all the time the quantum progress of NFL players between one and two. How different is it right now for you? Yeah, I think uh the game's just slowing down a little bit. Um not by much though. You still got a lot to learn. Still got a lot to improve. Um if anything, you just got 20some games now to go back and watch and figure out how you can improve and what to get better at. But I think JB um does a great job with kind of having me learn and grow every single day to be the player I want to be come uh the first game of the season. Is there any talk about what's going to be like around here with Ardos here this spring camp? >> Yeah, it's it's going to be fun. I think people are going to start to see um kind of our personalities come to light and and realize um how special this organization is and what we do here. And I think it's going to be a super cool opportunity for people to kind of get noticed um nationally about how awesome and high character they are. So, we're excited for it. You're you were new to the line last year with a couple new players. Now you got all five starters back, a lot of depth guys back. Just what can that do for an offensive line having that level of continuity? >> Yeah, it's it's it's really good to to like you said have that continuity in the offensive line. I think it's going to be great going from last year to this year cuz now uh there's not as much of a learning curve once you get into training camp. we kind of understand how everybody plays, uh the different sets people are going to take, the different angles and on the run scheme, and um it's it's great, but we uh constantly got to continue to improve. >> What was your biggest emphasis this off season? Your first full off season. >> Yeah. Um I think just just really understanding the the game, the offense a lot more. I mean, last year you come in and you're just completely swimming in the playbook. um and you're just trying to play ball and survive and and stay in front of your guy. This off seasonason it was more of um what type of footwork, what type of set, what type of hand placement can I be using on certain plays, understanding um if it's a fivestep drop or a sevenstep drop, um the the time and the angle and all that stuff. So, it it was good to have this off seasonason to improve and we're looking forward to this next year. How much does having a different playbook do you feel any difference there especially with coach Benton still being there or does it really feel very close to being the same? >> Yeah, I I would say it feels extremely close to being the same. Um he does an awesome job uh blending kind of his version with our version to to make it simple and easy for us to understand. And that's kudos to to Flurry for doing that. Um and he's an unbelievable coordinator as you can tell this spring. He's he's really brilliant in what he does and I'm super excited this uh this fall to get going. >> You and Jaylen take the Super Bowl rings back to North Dakota and show them off. >> No, I do got some other buddies in the NFL that are pretty pretty mad that year won it made it happen. But uh no, it's one of those deals. I'll probably wear it tonight and then throw it in the safe and move on to next year and go try and get that second one. >> What are you anxious most about the ring? The weight, the design? What what are you curious about? >> I want to know if like my hand is just going to completely fall down to my waist with how heavy it is. Um a lot of people are saying it's a big ring, but um it's one of those deals it's it's going to be cool to celebrate kind of put the final bow on uh this past season and then at the end day like it's June of 26. Like we got to start preparing for this next year and kind of understand we're a new team. um got a lot of new pieces and figure out how to win games this next year. >> A couple guys have mentioned that. How much do you guys appreciate bookending the offseason, being done with the offseason, doing the ring, and then it's almost a put it behind you launch point for this? >> Yeah, I what a better way um to kind of celebrate the end of OTAAS uh and mini camp than than to have this kind of party. Um, but I know there's a lot of guys on the team that are wishing they could come to it and they want to kind of get going to this next year so we can do this all over again next year. But, um, like you said, it's it's going to be great. We're going to have a ton of fun. Probably have a few bruskies in there tonight. Um, and enjoy each other and then like you said, just move on. >> Interested in the World Cup at all? Are you doing anything? >> God, I wish. Um, I think it's super cool for Seattle to have to have a game here, but like I was just telling these guys, I got to get home, get to work on the farm. Lot all the fun and plays been had out here during OTAAS. Now it's now it's time for the real work. >> Still got farm work today. >> Oh yeah. >> Too boring. Get out of that. >> No, even worse. It's like got even more rocks to pick and weeds to pull. It's going to be brutal. >> What are you doing when you go home? Six weeks. >> Yeah. Uh going to be spraying. Um got a got a feed lot. I got to build this off seasonason. So, told JB I'm going to be super excited come July 24th, 25th to get back out here and get back to football. So, um it's it's going to be a busy off season, lifting and and end up working on the farm. >> And you got the heat and humidity rolling in about now, right? I mean, >> yeah. Thanks for a reminder. [laughter] >> Yeah, >> completely off. Have you seen Rocky for by any chance? >> The Which one does he fight? Is it >> Drago? This is the one he's fighting Drago. Training in Russia. Yeah, absolutely. I wonder if he might adopt something like that. >> I Yeah, we might have to. I mean, I feel like there's some newer modern equipment I should probably be using. But what a training scene. Got to go back and watch that before this off season. But yeah, it should be fun. >> All right. >> All righty. Thanks, guys.

title: Abraham Lucas: "We're Picking Up Where We Left Off" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How you doing, Abe? >> Great. >> What do you What do you think tonight will be like in the ring and all that? >> Say that one more time? >> What do you think tonight will be feel like for you getting in the ring and all that? >> It'll be exciting. Um yeah, I mean, been looking forward to the day. Uh I also think it'll be a nice kind of like I mean, in my mind I've kind of moved forward a little bit, but this is like an official like cap off to last year and then like Mike says, run it forward to the next year. >> You mentioned that. That's the phrase Mike used earlier on. Seems like you've been hearing a similar version of it from players. How's that message kind of taking hold of the team? Last year was great, but you got to move forward. >> I think it's great. I mean, I I I really like I think it's a the epitome of like a championship team mindset that, you know, like you know, you did it, great, but you got to keep going, you know, there's no there's no time to really dillydally on it. I mean, you have events like this tonight that'll take place where you celebrate it, but um after tonight, it's not I mean, it's not going to matter for next year, you know. It's not going to matter really for next year at all, so excited to get back after it. >> Abe, now you're in your fifth year. How have you seen your leadership as far as the way that you lead the team, lead your unit? How have you seen that evolve here now at this stage of your career? >> Um I mean, when you come in the league, you got to earn your stripes a bit. Um I don't know. I mean, I've always tried to lead by example and just try to be a true professional about it and, you know, fortunate enough to have really qualified veterans both on offense and defense during my career here. I mean, really it's just about for me it's just about, you know, doing my job the best I can um and leading in that way. >> What can it do for an offensive line to return not just all five starters, but a lot of depth guys who filled in starting in place of injuries? I mean, depth wise you guys have a lot of help back. >> Yeah. Um I mean, I'm excited about it cuz like there's a lot of continuity in the room. Um kind of feel bad for Bo a little bit just being the only rook, but um I mean, he's taken to everybody well and everybody likes him, so um it's just nice to kind of like have the gang together, so to speak. Uh not have too much shuffling around or anything. Um and in that way we're able to really hit the ground running and you know, it helps not having to learn a whole total new system this year, you know, so we're all just kind of picking up where we left off and just continuing to go forward. >> What's up right for you like as a coach? >> Um seems very calculated. Um I don't know if I've ever heard him talk about anything else outside of football. Like when he's here, it's all it's all business for him, which is great. I mean, and he's a super smart guy, um knows the ins and outs of the offense, obviously, but down to the minute details and you can just tell the way he talks that he's he's a true professional coach. Um and so I'm excited to be playing in the system and having him, you know, call the shots. >> Does Bo Stevens get any breaks on rookie duties cuz he's the only one? >> Um depends on the duties. >> [snorts] >> Yeah. Yeah, we give him a little bit more grace. Like I said, like I mean, when Charles and I came in and we had um you know, Gabe Jackson and Austin Blyth and those guys, they they were really they weren't lenient lenient to us, but they weren't they weren't total you know what's either. Um so and I think that's kind of how me and Charles try to be as veterans, you know, we still give him a little bit of a hard time, you know, uh still make him earn his stripes a little bit, but um like I said, he's been taken to the room really well and doing what he's supposed to. >> How much did re-signing here change well, not change, but give him something of a a foundation for this off season knowing you're in their plans and it's for as far as you can see, you're in familiar home. >> Yeah, I mean, it definitely is a little bit there's a little bit of uh I guess breathing room, so to speak. Um and it made me just kind of be like, okay, like a little bit of a long-term security uh sort of thing. I don't really have to worry about that. Um you know, it's what I worked towards. Uh and then really my biggest thing when that whole thing was going down was like and even in the off season last year after the Super Bowl was watching the guys in my class just all get you know get paid and and do what was best for them and their family and I was so excited for those guys you know cuz you know those are the guys we came or I came in with and we knew that we had a special class after our rookie year really even before our rookie year so I was more focused on like being happy for them as opposed to just for myself. >> You mean you mean the team's rookie class the >> Yeah 22 22's class. >> Interested in World Cup and are you going to any of the matches >> Uh no and no. I don't I'm not I'm don't really watch soccer like that. Um I hope I hope the US does well. >> Thank you guys. Thanks man. >> Great big group.

title: Leonard Williams: "I'm Seeing Our Culture Elevate To Another Level" | Seattle Seahawks
text: That seemed like a pretty energetic practice. Do you think that's part of why there's the excitement around the team? >> I mean, honestly, I think that's we're excited, but I think that's just our culture. And I think that's what I love about us. I think regardless of the situation, regardless if we were getting our rings today or if, you know, it's the last day of practice before we're breaking for OTAs, I think we just play with passion and energy. We love each We love each other. We love coming to work. So, I think, you know, any any given day is like we're we're having those type of practices. >> You mentioned a reunion. We've seen some of the guys who were part of the work, you know, aren't here now, but who I assume are going to be back. What will that kind of be like seeing some of those guys? >> I mean, it's going to be cool. We all understand that this is a business and guys like come and go and, you know, that's that's the nature of the league, but you know, I hit up like, you know, Mafe and like Kobe Bryant and like some of those guys and know that they're going to be in town for tonight's ceremony. And, you know, we're all excited to see them and I'm sure it's going to feel like no time has passed. Like they're going to feel like a brother to us and I feel like it's going to be like that forever, regardless of where guys end up or even after football. >> Now that you're through mini camp, just how do you feel like this set of off season worked out for you guys? >> I mean, I feel like it's been great. It's been great attendance from the leaders, from the from the older guys. You know, young guys have been working hard like, you know, trying to be sponges of the game and learn as much as possible. And to me, I really just see our culture elevate to another level. I feel like last year, you know, we started putting the mix together and like all the ingredients and all that type of stuff and this year you really see it like boiling and and becoming more just of a foundation. And to me, the culture is the biggest thing that we need here. You know, guys are going to come and go like I said and I feel like if we have a culture and a foundation like that, you know, we'll always be a winning team. >> What's it like seeing new guys come in and get used to it or learn what it's all about? >> I mean, it's really cool. I mean, we get together in like small groups. We talk about it. We talk about the You could tell like young guys are just coming out of college. This is their first time in the NFL facility, first time in the NFL environment. But even they're speaking out about how it feels different here. The fact that young guys can feel that it goes to show that we really have something special. And um you know, it's on the big guy it's on the older guys and veterans also too hold everybody accountable to our standard. And you know, immediately like new guys come in and they they have to fall in line because that's just the expectation. >> The defense was basically historically good last year as was. Where do you feel like it can take another step though this year? What do you expect though? >> You try to ask for improvement out of what was already a really good >> I mean, I think just adapting to moving pieces. That's something about our defense that makes it great is we try to hold the pin last in all situations. So, you know, again like we're still we've been learning each other for like the last two years. You know, going on Mike's third year here people should have more of a grasp of the way he calls defenses, what type of defenses he's calling in certain situations. So, allowing us to play ahead of the snap pretty much is going to make you know, the more we diagnose the defense and and get used to all those moving pieces and changes is going to just allow us to play that much faster. >> You guys have basically the same defensive line for the most part that you had last year. Just the interior. What do you think about that continuity going into this season and where players like Riley Mills can fit in now moving forward? >> I mean, that's a a huge piece of it. You know, when I can trust the guy next to me, know the guy next to me, we play on a different tempo. We we sometimes could just look at each other and know what you know, how we're going to rush up front, how we're going to play blocks. That continuity is just huge. And you know, we just talked about how like guys come and go and stuff like that. But I think you know, we've done a good job here of like keeping majority of the same guys around each other and that allows for culture to grow in my opinion. >> And what about Riley Mills? Where do you think he can fit in and what kind of impact do you think he >> I mean, I think you're definitely going to see more plays from him, more game time from him this year. He's just looking a lot more uh, bouncy. You know, I know he was coming off of an injury um, his rookie season. He's He was doing a great job of like learning from the sideline and, you know, took his opportunity opportunity when he could. Um, but, you know, now going into OTAs, this is his first OTAs uh, in his second year and he just looks like more confident on his knee. Uh, just a little more confident as a player and uh, I think he's going to be a big help for us up front. >> What did you think of that sack, the play he made in the Super Bowl? What did you think of that? >> I mean, to me it just uh, goes to show like his potential. Um, you know, as soon as I met him and like seen his uh, you know, stature and like he's a big dude, like really strong dude. Um, the only thing that seemed to be holding him back a little bit was his knee injury, you know what I mean? He came back, started having practice and uh, you can tell he was like favoring one side and like you know, was coming off of a injury and uh, you know, that was a big moment for him in the Super Bowl to like get have that confidence at the end of his uh, rookie season and uh, that was a big time play and it it shows like what type of potential he has as a player and I think he's going to take it to another level. >> You've been teammates with Julian Love for almost all of his career in different spots. Like, how have you seen him just grow? Like, I know you guys call him the mayor now. Like, how have you seen him just grow into a leader he is? >> To me, he's always been that guy, which is so special in my opinion. Um, you know, I got you know, to the Giants his rookie year and he's been the same guy. Um, he's one of those guys that, you know, he has a process. He's going to show up to work uh, with enthusiasm every day and to me it's um, over time the the the biggest growth I've seen is everyone else noticing it. Um, and that's what's so cool is you know, he's he's finally getting his flowers. Uh, he has been for a few years now, I know that, but it's a cool for me to see, you know, someone that I've seen uh, as a young age grow into uh, a respected player in the league. And you know, we were just sharing about that, you know, the other day on at practice that, you know, we played it with each other for eight years now and uh, that's the longest I've ever played with anybody. >> Yeah, who came up with that nickname for you? >> What, the mayor? I'm not sure. It just I'm I'm pretty sure it starts in like team meetings and like defensive meetings like when he gets called out and like goes up to talk to the team and he speaks so, you know, so well up there. Everyone just starts saying, "That's the mayor. That's the mayor." Like it's pretty funny. I mean I think so. I think I'd be lying if I said there wasn't a little extra motivation from hearing that type of stuff. There's a little extra like chips on our shoulder. You know, we just came off of a Super Bowl you know, winning season and people are still you know, giving other people favorites over us. But at the same time like I said it's like it's always about us. It's about our process. I think that is still adding fuel to the fire for guys. But at the same time we're going to stick to our process regardless of what other people outside may think. Yeah, yeah. Uh I'm reading a book that AD just gave me actually. It's called Chop Wood Carry Water. It's pretty good. It's pretty much about how there was this construction I mean he was like a house builder in Japan and he was known for just his great work and great craftsmanship. He ends up retiring and then someone comes and takes him out of retirement asks him to build one last house. On that one last house he was uh He was cutting corners a little bit cuz he felt like you know, he had been retired. He was like comfortable. He's been already recognized for all his greatness and he decided to cut corners on this last house and that last house the guy who asked him to come out of retirement ends up giving him the key and saying that this is your house and so I think it's kind of a representation that you know, Uh, wanted to like talk to me and like some of the older guys on the team that, you know, even though we've had great careers and even though we've uh, got respect around the league and stuff like that, like how do we really want to like keep finishing our legacy? >> Do you know if anybody else is reading? >> Uh, yeah, I know like DeMarcus Lawrence and like Jay Reed, um, Chidobe, a few of us are reading it right now. >> I I don't think we've talked to you since you became a father. How How is all that going? >> I mean, it's been amazing. Uh, honestly, like I almost forget about the Super Bowl sometimes. It's been that amazing. Um, I'm blessed that we were able to have our kid after the season cuz I was actually able to be around and be super involved and like be there for the birth and all that stuff. Um, I'm sure that would be hard to like do all that type of stuff during season. Um, and I swear like most of the congratulations that I've been getting all off season have been about my son and family and I appreciate those things because I'm like, you know, this is what matters and uh, you know, sometimes I get reminded of the Super Bowl, but the having my son has been amazing. >> All right. Anything else? >> Okay. Thank you. Thank you.

title: Alex Anzalone, Jacob Parrish & More on Defensive Upgrades | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Good. >> Nobody's touching those long locks, huh? >> Uh, no. Not with not with it up. Not with it up. >> How are you enjoying things here in Tampa so far? >> It's good. It's good. I think that, um, you know, there's good understanding of what needs to be done, uh, schematically. I think that, um, you know, there a lot of young guys stepping up and kind of coming into their own.
