What have you seen from him and how much of a leap will that be if you guys are on the field together? >> Yeah. Um, no, he's a great player. Obviously, he has the pedigree. Um, I remember watching I grew up an Eagles fan, so I watched his dad growing up. Um, >> that had to be surreal for you then. >> I mean, you you grow out of that. you, you know, um, as you get older and go through the league for a little while. But, um, no, obviously he's a great player. Uh, second round draft pick and, um, you know, he has some learning to do and some growth to do and, uh, this is really good for him. I know he's getting some team reps now and, you know, training camp will be really big for him and his development. So, you know, as as soon as he can, you know, pick up the playbook and, you know, just see the different concepts and routes and, um, things you need to do as a linebacker, he'll he'll be even better and ready when season comes. It's pretty early on in the process, but how do you feel about top goals and defense? You've gotten a few reps. >> Yeah. >> Yeah, it's good. Um, you know, it took me a couple weeks to kind of really understand it or truly pick up on like the verbiage. It's everyone kind of runs similar things. Obviously, he has a little more complex system than uh what I'm used to, but um you know, it's it's been pretty it's been pretty easy to pick up and communicate and understand what he's trying to accomplish. I think for me as a linebacker, the biggest thing now is trying to see what he likes to call in certain situations and understand him as a play caller as opposed to the actual playbook. >> How are you able to use your length um out there on the field? I mean, we hear so often, you know, you're statistically one of the best coverage guys in the league and it shows up. But, but just being able to have that length and that height, how does that give you an advantage? >> Uh, I mean, yeah, it definitely does. I think, you know, it's you look at mismatches off offenses look for and um you know, the things a lot of tight ends around the league that they look at just because of their size and when you get a safety covering them, they they obviously have that the size advantage. And being a a longer athletic linebacker, I'm able to kind of do that role. And um you know, I know now I'm going to be asked to do a little bit more than that in the past. But um yeah, that's definitely a benefit and God-given. So, I'm I'm happy about that. >> We know you can run and we know you can tackle and cover, but how excited are you to be that guy that gets to place a few times? >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. I think that I'm definitely going to have some free runs at the quarterback and um you know, get some stats and force fumbles and things of that nature. So, as a linebacker, that's what you really want to want to do and make those splash plays and yeah, I'm excited for that. >> The front office clearly put a lot of resources in building up the front. Yeah. >> You guys sense that? You feel like that room obviously last year, but that room has significant. >> Yeah, you could you can kind of get a sense of um what a front office is trying to do as a player um and who they're bringing in, the types of guys they're bringing in and um you know, what they're trying to accomplish. So, I think that yeah, it's definitely a different mindset, I guess. And you know, I I haven't been here or like been a part of you know, whatever whatever personnel decisions and things like that. So, um, but I know this time we got, you know, guys that love to play football and play play the game with respect and play the game the right way. >> What's it like having a shot when you get feed out here? >> Yeah, >> obviously, you know. >> Yeah, it's great. It's great. You know, the the more uh the more the bigger the guys you have in front of you, the better. And obviously those guys aren't just big, they're athletic, too. So, um, they're going to be taking up double teams and, you know, allow us linebackers to float to the ball. >> What about a guy like that that has that type of attitude? came out here. He said, you know, that that he gets his edge from the fact that he was picked on as a kid and and um you know, it kind of gave him an mentality like to be able to play behind a guy like that like what does that do for you? >> Yeah, it's great. Um, you know, obviously pads haven't been on and um, you know, but you learn to play play the game off of each other and um, you know, it's that's definitely a great thing about OTAAS and and mini camp coming up is you learn like what guys like to do, what guys are thinking and um, especially the Dline as a as a linebacker that you need to know how the Dline likes to play and you know what blocks they like to play into and how they play into it. There are people walking up to Madison Square Garden just giddy taking pictures. You know, the New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown just happens to be a 49ers fan. >> Double win tonight for me. Brock Birdie put the team on his back, but the 49ers did a whole heck of a lot on both sides of the ball to finish off Detroit, but then they couldn't finish off the Super Bowl. So that comeback is not nearly as celebrated as it probably should be. I also think about the January 2003 NFC wildard game. The 49ers playing New York's team, the Giants down by a lot. You know, somebody who knows a thing or two about finishing the job here in New York because that's where the Seahawks won the Super Bowl in 2013, the 49ers linebackers coach KJ Wright. Now, physically 6'4, very similar to Jaden Duggar. Maybe not a 7 foot wingspan, but listen to KJ talking about the challenges facing the long rookie linebacker with his length. Grand Central Station, iconic, the next stop, not as tall as some of the buildings around it, but taller than the 49ers linebacker core, which by the way, exceptionally tall. They're looking for length to disrupt passing lanes. That's why I talk so much about the wingspan of Jaden Duggar. That's how KJ Wright played for the Seattle Seahawks. Height has some length. Height has some speed. And now the linebackers of the 49ers are trying to develop from Jaden Duggar to Larry Worth. They also have some length. The 49ers want to be like a basketball team in that front seven, but a physical one, one that can also play the run. And that's where coaching and development comes in. Because we have to discuss this, you know, in Raheem Morris terms, and that is talking about the adaptability of the whole front seven. Let's focus a little bit more on Romelo Height and Chris Cacerk. Let's bring in Chris Caceric, the 49ers defensive line coach. When I talked to him about height, it was interesting to me that the common theme that Chris Cacerk kept on returning to was speed. >> Yeah, speed, explosion. So, um you know, and then just the way he plays, the energy he brings, you know, when every time he put on the the Tech film last year, he was showing up around the ball, pursuing the ball across the field. Um obviously the pass rush jumps off the tape. So, and then just the toughness that he plays with. The 49ers believe in Romelo Heights pass rushing ability. That's obviously a given. But when you hear Cacerk talk, when you hear Raheem Morris talk, when you hear KJ Wright talk, I mean, coaches at multiple different positions, and I'm sure if we talked to Greg Scrugs, a Dline coach who's working with Romelo Height on his coverage drops, uh, we would notice that this pattern that they're all talking about the guy's speed, his ability to make grass disappear. And I think that's one of the biggest hints when it comes to our analysis of how this 49ers defense is going to be structured under Raheem Morris. He wants intense athleticism, high traits guys in that front seven. You saw the 49ers go after exceptional relative athletic scores, but above all else, he wants that length in the front seven to create true matchup problems for opposing offenses. Comes back down to some fiveman fronts. And you know, the 49ers, before we get too far carried away and say that they're going to radicalize this entire defense and uh change everything schematically, Chris Caceric made it very clear, and I think Raheem Morris has made it clear as well that the 49ers will stay in their base four down front. But what they're adding is the variability of the fiveman front because Raheem has experience with all of these different fronts. And that fiveman front would allow the 49ers and will allow the 49ers to execute some of these coverage drops and some of this adaptable play from defensive ends like Romelo Height. And I would say by extension even Jaden Duggar. Why? Why Duggar? Well, look at the positional background of Jaden Duggar. He played an edge rusher type position, something like Romelo Height before he moved to inside linebacker. Before then, Jaden Duggar was a safety. So, they're training him strictly as linebacker now to to get him used to playing in the fray against the run. That's going to be the base of Jaden Duggar's play. But, I think that you cannot ignore the fact that he's been at several different positions because the 49ers will naturally deploy their front seven players and some of these linebackers in a variety of different roles. That's what's going to make this scheme ultimately sing for San Francisco. So, this intense focus on length to play against the pass and this very ambitious plan to try to combine that length with run defense capabilities because we know the 49ers have to be good in that phase of the game as well. I mean, it's a tough needle to thread, but I think ultimately it is all potentially made possible by how big and strong a team is at defensive tackle. And that's the position that I'm going to talk about in our next video. As you can see, it's it's time to leave New York. That's why I'm at Grand Central Station. Have to head out to the airport. But so much of this 49ers defensive plan is rooted in what they can do right in the middle, right at that defensive tackle spot, which is why they've invested so much in the interior over the course of the past two seasons. Obviously, the draft with Alfred Collins, CJ West, and Grayson Halton. I would even say Mike Williams fits into the interior plan because he'll rush from there. But then the trade for OSA de Gazua this past year. If you are strong against both the run and the pass and probably run first, if you're strong against the run as a foundation on the interior and you could draw some double teams there, it opens up the flow for the linebacker position. It opens up the flow for the rest of the front seven to be able to capitalize on their comparative advantages. And for the 49ers, I think that very clearly is going to be height. From Fred Warner, the tall 6'4 linebacker brought aboard in 2018, an all-time great now to the rookies are going to be trying to make their names. The 49ers are doing something different in that front seven. But it all ends up being rooted in that defensive line, in that interior. And that's what the 49ers have maybe improved the most this offseason. So, subscribe because the next video we're going to talk about those defensive tackles and hear from Chris Cerak on them as well. So, long from New York City. It was a hell of a 24-hour stop and I think this is a good place to finish it. We'll see if the Knicks can finish the job after one of the great comebacks in sports history. Yeah. Heat.

Um he's instinctual then he's he's quick. He's really fast and um athletic as well. um you know he's my roommate during uh training camp and all that so we're pretty close and um it's nice to be able to pick his brain on the other side of the ball and him to pick mine as well. >> How is the competition in the receiving room helping you get better for your two? Yeah, I mean I think Iron Shreper's iron. Um, you know, we got a lot of guys who have different skill sets. Um, but they all have high character um different experiences and u you know they're fun to work with. They make um it fun to come into work and u we all want to be be you know better individually uh and compete individually, but at the same time we want to be the best group that we can be. >> Comes to the return game. You're not going to be surprised at anybody anymore. How are you going to handle that during the season? >> Uh I mean I think after week nine I wasn't surprised either. So, like it's the same thing. >> Last one. You good? >> Not afraid to use the tight end. Did so wherever he's been. Um there's been great clips of Gronowski, uh Dalton Concade, Dawson Knox, just uh just doing things that usually you see receivers do. So, being able to be uh worked into the offense like that has been uh it's been great. >> I just asked Taja the same question about getting Randy Jordan back. How big of a whistle for you guys to get stock back? >> Oh, for sure. I mean, that was my one of my first phone calls he called me and so I was uh I was fired up. Obviously, you saw what he was able to do with me throughout a whole NFL season last year. Um I feel super confident coming into this off season. Um he's really broken down the new offense for me. Um he's a he's a football wizard, so it's been uh it's been great to be in his room again. >> Last year you were just a rookie trying to find your way coming in at this point. This year obviously you know you're in a different position. If there's a mindset switch, how do you approach it differently knowing that a lot of the weight and the tight end pass the catching game from here? >> Yeah, I mean, I come in here just like a rookie. I mean, it's almost like a nothing to lose mindset. Um, cuz I, you know, play more free, I feel. Um, but as a rookie, to me, it really was nothing to lose. You know, it was a young team. Um, we didn't have the best record, so it was really just go out there and and do what you can. It's kind of the same mindset for me. Um, because that puts me in a mindset that go out there and play my best. you get to you get a little bit of a relationship going with Daniel during fighting you maybe. And what was it like to see him join the team and has been working with him? >> Yeah, absolutely. We go to uh we have the same offseason program, do the same combine prep stuff. So, I see him back here in the offseason quite a bit. Uh met him last year at tight end immediately. Just, you know, loved his personality. Such a great dude. Um so, you know, when I saw that we signed him, there was rumors of it. Uh I was hoping for it. You know, he's been around it for for a lot longer than I have. Um he's played a lot of football, so uh super blessed with the opportunity to work with him. I think we complement each other really well. >> What's the biggest thing you learned last year? And and what are some things you know you need to improve on? >> Uh definitely pad level, I would say, and and uh second level blocking and hand placement. I mean, uh honestly, there's there's room for improvement everywhere uh to me. And uh that's how I'm attacking this off seasonason. >> How excited are you and how much of a benefit is it? Because it seems like a lot of the teams around the league is starting to swing back. We're starting to see a lot more two and even three tight end sets around the league and the tight ends becoming more of a a weapon not only as run block but in the pass game. >> Yeah, it's been great. Obviously, we have a super stacked receiver room. Um you know, we got great chemistry on the field. So, you know, when you need a guy to to pop open, you know, you can rely on me, Dan, Kylin, DMR, really anyone in the room. So, uh it's been great. Um you know, around the league, everybody's got tight end tight ends in there, you know, doing different things. So, uh it's been good to see. It's been great to be a part of. Is there anything different to you about culture and the solid routine compared to what was being experienced last year? >> Yeah, absolutely. Um, you know, I think our culture already is super strong. Uh, and you could see that during practice. You know, we're just in OTAAS and every time you get out there to compete against the defense, it's been great. Um, guys are flying around making plays, being excited for one another. That just builds chemistry. Um, you know, we've had offensive dinners off the field. Um, I know defensive guys have done stuff off the field. So, you know, as as much as you can do off the field translate to on the field. >> Do anything bodywise different or whether it's diet, you know, trying to put on weight or anything you tried to change this off season? >> Definitely diet. Yeah, I mean, I think that helps just, you know, get in and out of breaks. Uh, get in and out of my stance. Um, doing a lot more lower body things. Uh, you know, building my core up as much as I can. So, um, I've had a good plan set in place, uh, good diet set in place, and, um, I was ready to attack the offseason when I came back. What did you learn from the first year about what it takes to be a sustained, consistent, successful tight end in the league? >> Yeah, I was taught uh last season. Um it's one of the things I live by is never count yourself in, never count yourself out. So, uh you know, that was kind of me last year. Um going back to, you know, kind of nothing to lose mentality. Um I learned that, uh you know, even as a rookie, um this year, you know, the position that I'm in, never count myself in. Um there's always something to uh to go out there and do, something out there to prove. Um, and there's somebody always coming for your spot. >> Couple more. You good? >> Thanks. >> Thank you guys. >> The opportunity that you have to maybe state your claim to the Nickelback job as a guy coming in here last year as a late round pick. >> Um, I think it's a great opportunity. Um, but I'm just attacking every situation the same way I do. Um, when I came in last year, just coming to work and accepting whatever role. >> How do you like having a designated nickel coach? Sorry. >> Sorry. nickel coach? Um, I enjoyed a lot. Me and Don, we do we have a lot of conversations on and off the field. Um, we're able to connect more and uh more in in depth about life in general and then also on the field. So, it's been great having a nickel coach. >> You look at some of the guys before like a Kiwan Williams or someone like that like how much does that excite you to be able to do some of the things seeing what they've been able to do in this game? >> Um, it's been very exciting. Um, I've actually sat down with Gus and watched a little bit of past Nicholls that he's coached. Um and then talked to to T0 about it a little bit and then Salah just about the success that the Nicholls have had in this system. So it's very exciting >> that that feel to be able to know anticipate the snap count but not sell it. How do you feel you're coming along to you know when you got to go in there? >> Yeah. Um I think I've um way better than last year for sure at uh tightening up the snap count just getting more comfortable and it just comes with reps just knowing when and and what's happening. >> What do you think biggest lessons learned from you in in year one? Um the speed of the game um is one thing I think for sure being able to adjust. Um but then also just I guess getting more comfortable with scheme and and and knowing my job and then also just being able to anticipate now instead of just reacting. >> What's how do you feel two as far as being ready or or being able to put yourself in a position to be ready? >> So far it's been good. Um still a lot of work to do. Um but I definitely feel a lot better going into year two obviously than year one. Seems like there have been days out here where you haven't come off the field once, twos, or threes. Is that your choice? Is that the coach's choice? Kind of why are you getting so many reps right now? >> Um, just getting out. I mean, nickel, we go nickel and base. So, we in nickel just trying to get as many nickel reps as possible. Um, it's really up to the coaches. It's not my choice. I just listen to what the coaches say and I go out there when it's my turn to play. >> The front office didn't draft a corner this year. What does that say about their belief in you and what you can provide this season? >> Um, obviously it's a it's a good thing. Um, but as you know in this business, like they could bring anybody in at any point. So, I mean, just keep my head down and working and not paying much attention to the outside. >> How much more confident comfortable do you feel now than a year ago? >> Uh, probably 10 times more confident. Um, obviously this I played a lot in the second half of the season. Um, and then coming into it, I've gotten a lot of reps um and gotten comfortable with the scheme, so I feel a lot more confident. >> What have your early impressions been on Alante Corale Josh some of the new faces in the room? Yeah, great guys that we added to the room. Um, very very confident men. Um, they've come they played a high level ball. Josh, I think two Super Bowls, so he's played a lot of football. Lone played a ton of snaps and and Cordell played a ton of snaps as well up in New York. So, I think they've been a great addition and and great veteran guys to help lead this room. >> Do you talk to Alante a lot about cuz he played a lot of nipples before he got here. Do you talk to him a lot about that? >> Uh, yeah, me and me and Lante, we talk a lot about um just inside and out. I played inside and out last year and just the uh the versatility, but we also have a lot of talks about nickel and I pick his brain about what he sees and that kind of thing and try to take some of that from his game. >> What's some of the feedback you got? >> Um just more about just like eliminating things and not worrying about certain things and then um on top of that just being confident in what you do knowing that the nickel is the one who unlocks the defense. So it's a pretty big role. >> Couple more. How would you describe the progress of the offensive guys in your class from last year to this time of the year? Uh, I mean it's been great. I mean, we worked out in the summer or not in the summer, just this offseason a little bit when we came back together a couple guys here. Um, but they they've been they've been growing and taking steps and getting more chemistry with Cam. >> You do anything different from a body standpoint this offseason as far as how you train size you want to get, I anything like that? >> Uh, no, not necessarily. I mean, I had more time. I wasn't doing the pre-draft process, so I had more time to focus on lifting and getting stronger and not training for a combine or a pro day. So, I've been, I guess, lifting a little bit more um and just getting more fitting for that nickel position. >> Lat. >> Uh, yeah. Being a young guy, I mean, you had a lot of success last year, you know, making a team and playing a lot of snaps, being role in this team. What was the biggest thing that you did off the field that you feel like helped you uh succeed in that role? >> Um, I think off the field, I mean, I was in my playbook heavy. Um, that was one thing, knowing your job is going to get you a shot to be on the field. Um, and knowing I wasn't getting a lot of reps on the field. So, a lot of my reps was in the meeting room or in walkthrough. So, just knowing my job and my role was probably the biggest thing I did off the field in order to have that kind of success when it was my turn >> season. What's the mindset as you prepare? And obviously there's a committee of you guys. How are you approaching? >> Um, just really taking one day at a time. Uh, building with my teammates. uh making sure uh just putting the best foot up for each and every day, making the days count. >> Change has been kind of common theme here the last couple years, but how nice was it for you guys to have Randy back on set? >> It was great. It was great. A lot of things changing around us and like our main center, our main piece at running back. We get our coach back. So, that's a blessing that we get to this our third consecutive year with him. So, we building a lot of steam going into the season. >> What's the biggest difference in the offense Dable's putting in as opposed to what you guys had the last couple years? Um it just seemed like more freedom. Um different places that uh we can get put in. Um just being able to be versatile and just go out there and freely play. >> You trying to think different this off season? What what are some things you maybe have done to kind of prepare for for what is this year four now? >> Mhm. Going on year four. Um, just investing into like myself, investing into my mental, also my body, just taking care of my body. Um, over the course of the offseason to lead me up until now and and when we get this break, do doing the same thing, but dialing it up some more. >> What's it like you missing range of being back, but you do have a lot of changes around, you know, dealing with new faces that coaching staff across the team. >> Um, can you ask can you can you ask that question one more time? What's it like as far as having to deal with so much change and kind of prove yourself all over again maybe to a new group? >> Well, in this league, you got to prove yourself each and every day, each and every year. But, um, like I said, it's great having Randy back cuz like we got our centerpiece. Um, he uh keeps us he keeps everything like co steady. He he keeps everything calm. He um he make it as simple as possible for us. But, um, with the change going around us, we just got to focus in on the day. Um, just focus in where we at. You caught a pass today and he had a Randy Jordan had a really he he reacted to it. He was excited. Do you feel that there's a degree of pass catching that that still is yet to be unlocked? >> Oh yeah. Um each and every day uh is I um evolve. So just evolving into like the player and also the man I'm supposed to be each and every day. So it's fun. I put myself in uncomfortable positions uh to get these results, but it's going to get done. A lot gets made about players in contract years. Just kind of how are you handling going into this last year in a contract? What's your mindset about the future? I guess >> consistency. Consistency overrules everything. So, if I'm if I'm uh like consistently up and down, that's what kind of results I'm going to get. So, like I'm trying to consistently improve. Some days some days it won't be that, but like long as I stay consistent inside of the person that I am and and the player that I am, everything going to be good. >> How's your relationship with Tony grown over the last couple years? Um, I feel like we hit our peak this year. That's my brother, man. Um, we text each other constantly and we always making sure we always making sure each other's safe and yeah, that's my brother. >> What do you make of Nick and the team so far? What he's adding to your guys? >> He's great. He um he's he works really hard. Um, he's a he's a a good addition to us and he's going to help us in the long run. >> How does that relationship with Tony do you think translates to positive things on the field? Um because um so I I feel like in order for you to tell someone something, you got to have a relationship with them. So he tell me like things that I need to improve on and vice versa. But I couldn't do I couldn't really we couldn't accept the criticism from each other if we don't have a relationship. So it starts with our relationship and I feel like we have a great one. >> You've been a part of a couple of tough tough a couple of tough years. What gives you hope that maybe things are about to turn? Um, I went through I went through never try to always look back and like try to correlate things together, but I went through the same things in college. So, my first few years in college was kind of rough. Dealing with injury, dealing with the record. So, eventually like we keep on working hard and we keep on like mounting together, eventually something got to change and it's the year to change. We got a new logo. We got a lot of new things around here. So, we gonna have a winning record this year. >> How do you like the new logo, new uniforms? >> It's great. It's great. these colors, these blues and these reds, all they, you know, it's good. Hey, we got to go win some game with win some games with them, though. >> Good. Anything else? >> Thanks, man. >> Super pumped. I mean, I had so much fun with them back in Buffalo a few years ago when I had the opportunity to come back with them. Pretty much a no-brainer. Uh, coming here working with Cam, working with Dabes and Shay. Uh, it's been a lot of fun so far. Um, getting back in the offense. It's a great scheme. Uh, Cam's done a great job picking it up. all the guys really diving into the books and uh um just really picking it up really quickly. So, we we've had a lot of fun. It's been awesome to reconnect with Daves and Shay. Uh we have a lot of fun, but we also put in the work, too. So, it's been good. >> What makes this game just follow? What makes this game so beneficial? >> Uh it's just player friendly. Uh there's completions out there to be had. Um he's he's going to call the game the way you like it. He's going to call the concepts the way you like it. and uh it's just evolved over the years and it's been proven everywhere he's been that uh they they put up points and it's very friendly for the quarterback. So um you you just got to dive in, know the execution, go out there, find completions, and it's it's a really fun system to play in. >> Dave had mentioned how he stresses seeing the game through the eyes of you guys. Your experience with him, hey, what are some of the things that he does to be able to >> just communication with him uh on a daily basis and weekly basis? um the concepts that you like, the plays that you're comfortable with. Um whether you like no huddle, the tempos, getting on the ball or huddling up, the play actions, all those concepts and everything that you're comfortable with, he's going to call those more for you and and he's going to mold the offense around what you like as a quarterback. So, I think he calls it differently for each quarterback that's out there. He calls it to our strengths and what we like. and we're still in the early phases of this thing, but as we go through the rest of OTAAS and mini camp, we'll continue to evolve and see uh what we like as a offense, what fits us uh as well as the quarterback. >> When when you weighed your options before coming here, what were some of the things you considered and why was this maybe aside from the connections a good fit for you? >> Yeah, for sure. It was pretty much I was I was going back to Buffalo or the opportunity arose when free agency opened to come here and uh it it was a tough decision but in the end I felt like it was right for me and my family just to take this opportunity to come here and uh really reunite with Dabes and Shay. Uh but also I'm at the point in my career where I feel like I have a lot to offer as a mentor and K being young um we've had a great relationship so far and I'm really looking forward to helping him um in any way I can and and just take the next step and continue to help these young guys. Not only can Cam but everyone on this team it's a fairly young team overall. Um I'm getting up there with with my experience, but I feel like I have a lot to offer. I love being a great teammate. I love working hard out here coming out here and just uh throwing the ball around. So, it was a great opportunity to come here and uh I'm excited to play for coach Sala and uh and coach Daves. >> You've been in position before dealing with the pressure of being a young topic quarterback. Just what advice or what tips do you give him about handling all the noise, all the stuff you have to deal with? >> We don't really talk about the pressure and everything like that because he's a mature kid. I mean, that's that's understood when not only when you're picked high, but when you're in the quarterback position overall. Like, it's a scrutinized position. Um it's the most scrutinized position in sports. That's just what comes with it. That's that's just the job description. But you just got to block that stuff out. And at the end of the day, I think first and foremost, just be thankful that we have the opportunity to come out here and play football at the highest level, which is a blessing to do. So, you just go about your business. Uh you grind, you work a tail off, which he is, which we are in the quarterback room. We're all working, getting better. We're pushing each other. And uh I think everything else will take care of itself. But um it's it's it's not just one individual who needs to take the next step. It's it's everybody everybody around. we all got to take the next step as a unit, um, as a staff, as a whole, and I I like where we're headed in the right direction. Uh, just grinding throughout training camp and taking those next steps. >> What's a ballpark percentage of how much is new to you that you're learning right now? Like, how far ahead mentally are you from the rest of the guys learning it for the first time? >> Um, I think that would be hard to say. I would definitely say the the playbook has evolved from the last time I was in it. So there is a lot of new stuff, but I think the base and the core um has somewhat stayed the same, which has allowed me to um help the guys and so and so be be ahead a little bit mentally. Um it's helped me play faster and I know just like as a player when you know the system, you're able to go out there and play faster. So that's why I keep emphasizing to all these guys be like I I know it's a lot of information right now, but you if you get this stuff down, if you know exactly what your job description is, when you get onto the field, you're able to go out there and execute that much quicker. and I think they've really taken that to heart and the guys are playing fast out there and it's a lot of information but I think they're doing a great job with it. >> What's been your take on Bill getting to know him so far? >> Well, it's been great. I mean, all the guys in the quarterback room, I didn't know them coming into this, but it's it's been a lot of fun getting to know all of them. I mean, we've been out to dinner a couple times. Uh we hang out a lot in the quarterback room. Will, uh Cam, and Henden, all great dudes. I think they all got uh really good arms and and we're all all out here pushing each other. Um, I I like I like how they they come they come in and they work. They're professionals. Everyone's pushing each other. Everyone's got a good attitude. Um, we're not really talking about everything on the outside. We're just here to work. We're just here to push each other and continue to get better. I think everybody's done a great job coming in with a great attitude, having fun, and and putting their best foot forward. >> The receivers on this team or maybe some of the weapons overall. >> I think we got a lot of talent. I think um I I like the guys that we have. A lot of guys have been making plays and uh it's our job as quarterback to just give those guys opportunities. We got a lot of talent on the outside. A lot of speed I think um at receiver, tight end, and running back, a lot of dynamic playmakers. So, it's going to be interesting to see how we use these concepts, how we use these schemes to get these guys in open field and allow them to make plays and use their talents. >> What's the adjustment like for you when you know the system pretty much because you've been in it before, but you're working with guys you've never thrown to before. What's what's that like trying to get on the same page with them? >> I mean, that's like that's like you do that before every season, you know, like uh anytime you take a break and you come back to OTAAS and training camp the offseason, it's just like you're taking that time to to get the timing down. So, it's just reps on the field. Um everybody getting the execution, getting to know each other, getting to know the body language, their demeanor, getting in and out of cuts, and getting down the timing. So, um you just keep working, keep throwing with the guys, keep being consistent in your footwork and and where you're putting the ball. Um, and that that that will come all the timing and the repetition. >> You talked about what you like about Dave's scheme. Just as a quarterback playing for him, what's what's that like and how does he operate with that relationship? >> It's awesome. I think the the best thing I mean that he really does as a offensive coordinator, as a coordinator, is that he believes in you as a quarterback, as a player, as his talents, and he's like whoever he has, he's going to maximize those talents the most. And when your offensive coordinator has confidence in your ability, you're able to just go out there and sling it. It doesn't even matter at that point. You can call whatever. If if that guy believes in you, you go out there. Uh you'll make the concepts work and and we got a lot of playmakers. So, it's you just got to get those guys the ball and let them do their job. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Robert Saleh on Cam Ward: “We’re in Really Good Hands” | Titans Press Conference
text: So, Robert, as you're wrapping up this uh voluntary portion of of of the offseason, how has attendance been? How has communication been with guys who haven't been here maybe regularly? >> Yeah, everything's been good. I feel like we've had really good attendance. Um, you know, this time of year for in the football world, a lot of lot of babies get born, all that good stuff. So, some guys have been missing stuff and uh uh but overall attendance has been really good. How do you >> like progress? Just what you've seen on the field. progress from what from beginning >> it's for first year obviously new regime new schemes and all that stuff I think guys have done a really good job uh understanding what's being asked out of them um you know like I've said before a lot of this is taken with a grain of salt because once pads come on it gets faster uh gets a little bit harder so uh but but overall it's been good >> how do you feel Cam Ward has been I know the last couple days there's been some accuracy but there's situations that kind of dictated that but how do you feel he's been >> I think he's been great. You know, like this is the time of year where where he's got to try some things. He's got to see what he can and can't do. And uh and then you mix that in with a with a whole new scheme. Like um like I I I think it's I I mean I'll put myself out there. I think it's very safe to say that we've we've got a really really really good quarterback and uh and we're in really good hands. >> Are practices designed to challenge him or to make him respond to what he had to do the previous day again? Anyway, if you kind of let us in on how he's building dayto day. >> Yeah. Um, you know, day ball does a great job. They've they they're scripting it in a way that gets the entire offense better. Um, you know, we're making sure that he gets a chance to see every single look. So, we've I don't know if you guys have been out here, but we've had a lot of walkthroughs also, uh, where he basically gets the reps of everybody of the of the ones that he didn't get when the twos and threes are up. Um, you know, so we're trying to get him as many looks as possible. We're trying to make sure that he sees everything and um um but but every day regardless of which we're always going to try to challenge every player on this football team. >> Based on what you've seen so far, is there any urgency at this point to look for veteran depth? Um assign veteran depth before training camp begins >> at at any position. >> Any position? >> Anytime. I guess that's that's where I think Borggo is great. like we're um you're always constantly evaluating the roster and and where we're at and if you feel like there's an uh area where you can get better and there's a player out there that can make us better, you're always going to try to uh pursue that. >> If if Cam becomes what you guys think he can become, what do you think the one or two traits he can hang his hat on as these are the things that he does in the elite level are? Um, God, man. I, you know, I don't I don't know if I want to answer that one right now cuz I'm still learning him, too. Um, but I could tell you just visually just being out here with him, like he's got an unbelievable mindset. Um, he is fearless. Uh, he he's he really can move on to the next play no matter what happens the play before. His arm talent is ridiculous. um you know so as he continues to develop and his communication with Dave ball too like he's he's been awesome in that regard but uh he's a playmaker like in all our move the ball periods when we go unscripted I think that's where he shines the most um and I think he shines in those moments because it's he's just playing football you know and uh um you know so it's it's exciting to see him kind of develop through these OTAAS and it's exciting to see where he excels during the during the course of practice but um But once training camp gets going, I think we'll really see where he's at. >> To that end, obviously you're involved on a granular level, but just for this time of year taking the the opportunity to make this more observational than anything else. How important is that? >> I I think it's very important and and it's really all the time, you know, like I I spend most of my time on the football field talking to the coaches and trying to educ uh what I see so they can go fix it. Um, and then same thing in the meeting rooms. Just always doing my best to coach coaches and I'll talk to the players when I need to, but uh, you know, you're always trying to take a more of a global, at least speaking for me, just more of a global look at it to make sure that guys are all on the same page. We're speaking the same language. Um, and look, coaches have uh, position coaches have 10, 15 guys that they're dealing with. They might miss something. And that's having an extra set of eyes over there just to make sure that we're we're all protecting one another's blind spots. That's where I kind of try to try to fit in from uh uh from that perspective. And then once we get in the meeting rooms, we're we're all watching film together. We're scheming together and we're coming up with the plan together. >> What are you seeing out of Nick Singleton so far in in the OTAAS? And how is he kind of finding a role alongside of Tony and Taj? >> Um early obviously. Um big back fast. Uh he's learning it all. He's got a long way to go from that regard. Like all rookies do, but um um but to be clear, Tony and Taj are are the are the Bells of this football team and and Nick's got to compete his way in to find his way into that group. >> Greatly we see him in Indie, but then when you guys go to Skellyy and team, he's on the side field. Are you guys like are you monitoring anything in particular with him or how is that process coming along? How >> about Nick? >> Uh Calvin Ridley. >> Oh, really? Oh. Um, yeah, he's he's coming off of a uh uh an injury and we're just trying to make sure we progress him uh in the way that we need to. I think he's going to get some seven on seven reps today. So, it's just part of the protocol to get him uh uh to where he's comfortable with where uh with his body. >> What do you think the I guess distribution of carries or play time looks like for Tony and Taj or does that depend on maybe who's got the hot hand in games? Um, we'll decide that as as time goes. But, uh, those two complement each other very very well. Um, you know, they're both really really good third down backs. title: Bengals HC Zac Taylor Talks New-Look Defense, Burrow & More with Rich Eisen | Full Interview
text: Oh, the coach of the Cincinnati Bengals, Zac Taylor's back on the program. He is ready to to join us. Good to see you, coach. How are you? >> Good to see you, Rich. I'm doing great. Thanks for having me [applause] on. >> You bet. Um not to jump out of your lane to start, but did you watch NBA Finals action last night? Did you get a chance to do something like that? Or no? >> I think I I went to sleep. It was 70-something to 40-something. >> Mhm. >> And I woke up, um checked my phone and there was a minute left. So, I I pulled up the app on my phone and watched the rest of it. It was a It was a great ending. >> Yeah. So, you did So, let me get this straight. You you hit You hit shut eye, right? >> Yep. >> And then you popped awake. >> And then >> Just >> you checked your phone and you're like you got like you don't think you're going to like mess with your sleep pattern or anything like that, Zac? >> Well, I mean, it it just You know, it was amazing cuz when I was watching it, the game was over. There was no chance. >> That's correct. >> And so, when I saw that, I I think New York was was up one and then San Antonio hit two free throws. I ran down to my son's room. It was It was about midnight, I think, our time. What, >> right. >> He was asleep. I was going to wake him up and make him watch it, but >> How old is he? How old is he? >> He's going to be a freshman in high school. >> Okay. Yeah. No wonder you're getting your sleep. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. >> No wonder you're getting your shut eye. So, that was that was my reminder right there that um the game is never out of hand. You're always in it. But I was more fascinated with the end of game um scheme that was going on. You know, some of the plays they were drawn up on those last two possessions. Um and then just a small thing like getting a tip on the final inbounds pass and affected it cuz otherwise it looked like, you know, it's the play after the one you're showing here. >> Um where he he got his hand, you know, on the tip as it was inbounded. One time we came through and we won, went to the Super Bowl. The other time we we didn't and we lost. And so, I know the feeling on both sides. Uh the agony of defeat and the joy of the victory. Do you like how collaborative are you with Joe with Burrow? And which one does Joe like?
